papers.abstract_en: The classical density-wave scenario predicts a blue-to-red age--colour gradient across the spiral arms of disc galaxies as a consequence of shock-induced star formation. However, observations of spiral-arm pitch angles at different wavelengths sometimes suggest the opposite trend, namely a red-to-blue ``colour jump''. The origin of this apparent contradiction remains unclear. In this work, we investigate the effects of dust attenuation on post-shock stellar emission, together with the streamline motions of gas and stellar populations. We find that dust attenuation in regions with relatively high optical depths, $\hatτ_{V} \gtrsim 0.2$, can produce an apparent red-to-blue spatial sequence, with respect to the shock location, by reversing the relative positions of the flux maxima of stellar populations observed in different bands. Moreover, streamline motions confine post-shock stellar populations near the spiral arms for longer than in a circular-orbit model, thereby modifying the spatial distribution of the emitted light. We conclude that the apparent red-to-blue colour jump does not necessarily contradict the classical density-wave scenario. Instead, it can arise from the same post-shock stellar populations that intrinsically produce a blue-to-red age--colour gradient if their emission is modified by dust attenuation.

papers.title_en: Generalized Toric Threefolds from Scattering Diagrams and Broken Lines
papers.abstract_en: We present an explicit and practical description of Generalized Toric Calabi--Yau threefolds, which are associated with five-brane webs ending on seven-branes, using scattering diagrams and broken lines, based on ideas from arXiv:2410.04714 [hep-th]. Local theta-function algebras and their transition maps give explicit affine charts for opened (resolved) webs, extending familiar toric constructions to non-toric situations. We give a physical interpretation of the deformation parameters, in the case of one or several 7-branes, and deduce behavior under Hanany-Witten transitions and changes of tesselation.

papers.title_en: Lightest and heaviest nuclei as keys to the origin of ultrahigh energy cosmic rays
papers.abstract_en: The origin of ultrahigh energy cosmic rays (UHECRs) has been a long-standing mystery. A unique feature of UHECRs originating in binary neutron star mergers (BNSMs) is two distinct populations of light elements -- those directly accelerated in the jets, and photo-disintegration products of massive nuclei accelerated in the bulk outflow. We show that Pierre Auger Observatory spectrum and composition data confirm the existence of the predicted two populations at $\geq \!7.2σ$ significance, having rigidity ($R\equiv E/Ze$) cutoffs agreeing with prior estimates. The data also favor 5-10% of UHECRs originating as r-process nuclei, a signature of a BNSM origin. Our results provide strong evidence that UHECRs are produced by merging neutron stars, and show how UHECRs and UHE-neutrinos elucidate otherwise inaccessible aspects of neutron star mergers.

papers.title_en: Intranight optical monitoring of eight quasars with superluminal jets and low optical polarization: Probing the mechanism of rapid flux variability
papers.abstract_en: Intranight optical variability (INOV) of blazars whose emission arises predominantly from a relativistic jet, has been widely linked to a combination of two key observational diagnostics: the fractional optical polarization ($P_{opt}$) and the Doppler boost arising from relativistic beaming of the jet's emission. To discern which of these two factors plays the dominant role, we investigate INOV of a well-defined representative sample of 8 flat-spectrum radio quasars (FSRQs, which are `low-synchrotron-peaked' blazars) whose jets exhibit a low degree of polarization ($P_{opt}$ < 3$\%$) but a large superluminal motion with c$β_{app}$ = 5c $-$ 31c (median = 10c). We report sensitive optical monitoring of these 8 `low-polarization superluminal quasars' (LPSQs) using a 1.3-metre telescope, in 20 sessions of minimum 3-hour duration. These data were supplemented with similarly high-quality monitoring data/results available in the literature for this sample, thus adding another 19 sessions. Duty cycle (DC) of strong INOV (amplitude $ψ> 5\%$) is found to be zero, applying the normally used $F_η$ test, and $\sim 7\%$ using the more powerful `enhanced $F$-test'. The small DC, despite the strong Doppler boost expected from the observed high superluminality, shows that strong INOV is much rarer among LPSQs, compared to high-polarization quasars, for which DC $(ψ> 5\%$) is found to be around 30%, even using the $F_η$ test. This provides the first compelling evidence that optical polarization is the primary diagnostic of INOV, while relativistic beaming plays a supportive role. Possible implications for the proposed mechanisms for INOV are pointed out.

papers.title_en: The Halperin (111) state as a paired composite-fermion wave function: Two exact finite-size identities on the sphere
papers.abstract_en: Two wavefunctions have previously been proposed to describe the $ν=1/2+1/2$ quantum Hall bilayer: $p$-wave pairing of composite fermions and $s$-wave pairing of composite fermions with anti-composite fermions. We show analytically in the spherical geometry and within the Jain-Kamilla lowest Landau level projection scheme that both of these paired composite fermion wavefunctions exactly reproduce the Halperin (111) state for a specific form of the pairing that we derive. We also find a second wavefunction that is common between both classes of wavefunctions. However, we provide evidence the two variational families generate overlapping but not identical sets of electronic states, ruling out a universal reparametrization that identifies their wavefunctions.

papers.title_en: Exhaustive Construction of Generalized Parent Hamiltonians for Matrix Product States
papers.abstract_en: Characterizing local Hamiltonians that host interesting many-body states as eigenstates has been an important problem in quantum many-body physics. For matrix product states (MPS), there is a well-known construction of parent Hamiltonians that have the MPS as the frustration-free ground state. However, recent results on quantum many-body scars have shown that such a construction does not exhaust all possible Hamiltonians that have the MPS as an eigenstate. In this work, we develop an exhaustive construction of generalized parent Hamiltonians that have a given translation-invariant MPS as an eigenstate. These go beyond the conventional projector-based construction of frustration-free parent Hamiltonians, where each local Hermitian term has the MPS as an eigenstate, by allowing non-Hermitian telescoping terms that cancel out with periodic boundary conditions (PBC). We derive a local tensor equation that establishes a correspondence between inequivalent classes of generalized parent Hamiltonians, i.e., those that cannot be related using linear combinations with frustration-free Hamiltonians, and the MPS transfer matrix spectrum. We illustrate the connection to intrinsic physical properties, including non-Abelian symmetries and zero correlation length, and further extend this construction to block-injective MPS. Our framework hence provides a systematic bridge between generalized parent Hamiltonians and the local structure of quantum states.

papers.title_en: Hidden Neutrino Active Galaxy Candidates: Prospects for Catalog and Stacking Searches with IceCube, IceCube-Gen2, and KM3NeT
papers.abstract_en: In high-energy neutrino astrophysics, the identification of high-energy neutrino sources is a central goal, and jet-quiet active galactic nuclei (AGNs) have emerged as promising candidates. For this purpose, we present a theory-guided, intrinsic X-ray selected sample of hidden neutrino AGN candidates consisting of $28$ X-ray bright AGNs (X-HiNAC), combining the {\em Swift}/BAT and BASS surveys with dedicated {\em NuSTAR} observations and spectral analyses. We compile their intrinsic X-ray fluxes, spectral properties, luminosity distances, and supermassive black hole masses, to provide a coherent sample for neutrino source searches. The sample is physically motivated but remains model independent given that the neutrino flux is proportional to the intrinsic X-ray flux. Using the magnetically powered corona model, we also demonstrate the prospects for individual-source and stacking searches with IceCube-Gen2 and KM3NeT. We identify promising individual targets and find that stacking the remaining sources, excluding NGC 1068, could yield a $5σ$ detection within $\sim 5-15$ years under favorable model assumptions at the current and upcoming neutrino observatories. We highlight systematic uncertainties in the adopted source parameters, particularly the black hole masses, for which different measurement techniques can yield estimates differing by up to an order of magnitude. Such uncertainties can significantly affect the predicted neutrino emission, motivating more precise black hole mass measurements and improved broadband X-ray observations. Our findings motivate improved multiwavelength characterization of nearby AGNs and provide a guide for investigating their role as high-energy neutrino sources.

papers.title_en: Non-Invertible Charges for M-Theory
papers.abstract_en: The gauge charges of M-theory M2 and M5 branes almost resemble the charges of a 6-group. The charges of such a 6-group are expected to be modeled by operators with non-invertible fusion. We here consider non-invertible charge defects for continuous 2-groups and 6-groups, aiming to capture the gauge charges of M2 and M5 branes. We find a model for charges of a "pseudo 6-group" $\frak{G}$ which possesses remarkable similarities with known features of M2 and M5 branes, including: Hanany-Witten moves, the $\frak{a}_{N-1}$ charges, higher-form symmetry, and singleton decomposition of M5-brane worldvolume theories, and couplings of M5/anti-M5 states.

papers.title_en: Tests of an EP-Preserving Wake Force
papers.abstract_en: A universal quadratic coupling of ultralight scalar dark matter to ordinary matter preserves the weak equivalence principle for unscreened point particles. A finite test body is nevertheless not a passive probe: it distorts the scalar field that accelerates it. We show that this field distortion produces a differential acceleration between concentric test masses, even when their microscopic coupling is universal. We calculate this signal including how each test mass distorts the field acting on the other, deriving the weak-screening limit and extending the calculation to stronger screening using concentric spherical layers. Applying the model to MICROSCOPE, we find differential signals in both its equivalence-principle sensor SUEP, whose test masses have different compositions, and its reference sensor SUREF, whose test masses have the same composition. We combine both sensors with the dark matter wake near Earth to recast the published MICROSCOPE measurements. Within this model, existing measurements probe scalar masses up to approximately $8 \times 10^{-9}\,$eV and couplings below the supernova bound. An analysis using the additional frequency components of the scalar signal could extend the mass reach and probe couplings below the BBN bound.

papers.title_en: The Multi-trace Eigenstate Thermalization Hypothesis
papers.abstract_en: We introduce a multi-trace eigenstate thermalization hypothesis, an extension of ETH that governs connected correlations of operator matrix elements with arbitrary index structures, including several disjoint index cycles. We derive multi-trace ETH from local rotational invariance, relate its independent data to higher-order free cumulants, and construct a cyclic matrix model that encodes the resulting multi-cycle data. We provide evidence for multi-trace ETH in chaotic quantum systems and compute multi-trace correlations in low-dimensional gravity. In few-body systems, multi-trace contributions arise from correlated periodic orbits, including a linear ramp contribution to the one-point spectral form factor. In two dimensions, we compute interaction-induced multi-trace correlations from a quartically coupled bulk scalar in JT gravity, relating winding matter diagrams to corrections of matter-channel weights and anomalous dimensions. In three dimensions, we show that multi-trace non-Gaussianities arise from both topology-changing saddles and light matter. Using Virasoro TQFT and conformal mean-field theory, we compute examples involving knot and link complements and torus wormholes with matter loops. Across these settings, multi-trace ETH provides a common framework for both connected correlators in chaotic quantum systems and multi-boundary wormhole amplitudes in gravity.

papers.title_en: Model-Independent Assessments of Tidal Alignment and Density-Weighting Dependence in Galaxy Intrinsic Alignments
papers.abstract_en: Intrinsic alignments (IA) of galaxies are an important source of systematic uncertainty in weak gravitational lensing measurements and also serve as a test for models of galaxy formation and evolution. These galaxy alignments are usually modeled assuming that the IA are sourced by the tidal fields around the galaxies. However, galaxy properties, like their proximity to other galaxies and their mass, provide alignment contributions beyond the tidal field. In this work, we perform novel model-agnostic tests to determine the impact of density-weighting on the IA of galaxies using data from the IllustrisTNG cosmological hydrodynamical simulation and SDSS-III (BOSS). We show that the primary effect of density-weighting is an increase of the alignment amplitude at large scales, whereas the small-scale impact is sample-dependent. We also assess the tidal alignment paradigm for IllustrisTNG galaxies using two-point correlation functions of galaxy shapes, tidal fields, and the sampled background tidal field of the simulation box. We find, given the precision of our measurements, that central galaxies align linearly to the underlying (non-linear) tidal field well into the 1-halo regime.

papers.title_en: An efficient approach to resistive GRMHD simulations of binary neutron star mergers
papers.abstract_en: Astrophysical plasmas are often highly conducting, but finite resistivity can nevertheless influence the evolution of strongly magnetised systems. Capturing these effects in general relativistic magnetohydrodynamics is computationally challenging because high conductivity leads to stiff source terms in the evolution equations. Standard numerical approaches rely on implicit-explicit (IMEX) time integration to maintain stability, but this substantially increases the complexity and computational cost of the simulations. Building upon the previously developed Resistive Extension upGrade for Ideal MagnEtohydrodynamics (REGIME), we present a new fluid-frame formulation that simplifies the incorporation of leading-order resistive effects by avoiding matrix inversions required in previous approaches. The method is implemented in a general relativistic magnetohydrodynamics code and validated through one-dimensional current-sheet tests and simulations of isolated magnetised neutron stars and binary neutron star mergers. We find that the new formulation reproduces the expected resistive behaviour with accuracy comparable to IMEX-based methods, while substantially reducing the computational cost and complexity of the simulations. In binary neutron star mergers, finite resistivity leads to measurable differences in the post-merger gravitational-wave signal and remnant structure, showing that resistive effects can produce measurable changes in the post-merger dynamics even in the high-conductivity regime.

papers.title_en: Baker--Akhiezer sections from Higgs bundles and Landau levels in hyperbolic band theory
papers.abstract_en: As observed by Kienzle and the second author, rank-two $\mathcal{O}(3)$-twisted Higgs bundles on the projective line encode all hyperbolic crystals of genus two: the spectral curves are the unit cells, and the Hitchin fibers are the abelian Brillouin zones. In a uniform magnetic field of two flux quanta, the lowest Landau level is one-dimensional at every nonzero momentum, and, as found by Iengo and Li, its dimension jumps to two at the zero momentum. We identify the states of the lowest Landau level with the Baker--Akhiezer sections of the Higgs bundles, and their zeros, the vortices, with the Baker--Akhiezer divisors. A family of nonzero momenta limits to the zero momentum exactly when each of the two vortices approaches the image of the other under the spatial inversion, and the states of the jumped level are labeled by the directions of limiting. On the Higgs bundle side, the zero momentum is the point where the Hitchin fiber intersects the Hitchin section. Such a family of Higgs bundles limits to the Hitchin section, thereby crossing to a lower stratum of the \BB stratification, an example of the phenomenon investigated in terms of Baker--Akhiezer divisors by the first author with Figiel and Teschner.

papers.title_en: Nova V1674 Her as a fast magnetic rotator
papers.abstract_en: We report on the results of our XMM-Newton and NuSTAR campaign targeting V1674 Her in October 2023. These observations were timed to investigate the post-nova quiescent state 28 months after the 2021 outburst, although the optical luminosity was still slowly declining. The X-ray spectra are well-modeled by a multi-temperature thermal plasma. While in the best fit temperature we find that the highest plasma temperature is indicative of a massive white dwarf ($M_{\text{WD}} \approx 1.35 M_\odot$), we caution that there is a degeneracy between the plasma temperature and the metallicity in the spectral fit, hindering a definitive constraint. Alternatively, the continuum can be phenomenologically described by a Comptonized component, although this model neglects the thermal bremsstrahlung component. Timing analysis reveals a stable 501.31 $\pm$ 0.19 s modulation in the post-quiescent phase, whose amplitude diminishes with increasing energy; this is quite typical in intermediate polars (IP). The phase alignment between the quiescent and early post-outburst Chandra spin-folded light curves suggests that the soft X-ray emission originates from the same polar regions, which quickly re-established accretion following the eruption. V1674 Her belongs to a growing class of novae that are also IPs, and is one of four in which the modulation with rotation was observed during the outburst supersoft X-ray phase. We propose that the fast rise in outburst was due to a fast or centrifugal magnetic rotator wind, causing rapid mass loss instead of the commonly assumed radiation pressure wind.

papers.title_en: Resolving the spinon hierarchy of the Heisenberg antiferromagnet
papers.abstract_en: A local spin fluctuation in the spin-$\tfrac12$ Heisenberg antiferromagnet creates an even number of fractional spinon excitations. We resolve its zero-temperature dynamical structure factor through six spinons directly in the thermodynamic limit. Beyond the established two-spinon contribution of $72.89\%$, the four-spinon response gives approximately $21.90\%$ of the integrated intensity and six spinons contribute a further $4.3\%$, bringing the response to about $99\%$ of both the intensity and first-frequency-moment sum rules. We derive momentum-independent first-moment fractions in the calculated sectors and a general upper-edge law $S_n\sim A_n(k)(ω_{n,u}-ω)^{(n^2-3)/2}$ for every even $n$ at nonzero momentum. The rapid growth of the edge exponent explains why the expanding multiparticle bandwidth carries very little high-energy weight, while higher sectors remain appreciable within the lower-sector continua.

papers.title_en: Chiral Majorana hinge modes on a curved surface with magnetic impurities
papers.abstract_en: Chiral Majorana modes, a key ingredient for topological quantum computation, arise on the surface of a three-dimensional time-reversal-invariant topological superconductor when a magnetic field induces a sign-changing surface mass. In practice, the orbital response of the superconductor tilts the surface spectrum and overwhelms the Zeeman term as the field grows. Here we show that magnetic impurities on a spherical surface can instead generate this mass term through their exchange coupling, so that only a weak field is required. The Ising surface Majorana modes mediate a ferromagnetic Ruderman-Kittel-Kasuya-Yosida (RKKY) interaction, derived here on the curved surface, that orders the radial impurity moments into an inversion-breaking hedgehog at zero field. An axial field instead stabilizes a domain wall across which the radial magnetization reverses sign, leaving a single chiral Majorana mode along the equator and realizing an inversion-protected second-order topological superconductor.

papers.title_en: Charge Pumping Leptogenesis from the Symmetric Mass Generation Phase on a Four-Leg Ladder Lattice
papers.abstract_en: Quantized charge pumping in quantum Hall systems is a bulk topological property, typically manifesting on gapless boundaries as spectral flow through chiral edge modes upon flux insertion. When the boundary is anomaly-free, it can be symmetrically gapped by symmetric mass generation (SMG) interactions. However, the effects on quantized charge pumping at an interacting gapped boundary are unclear. We address this using density-matrix renormalization group simulations of a four-leg ladder quasi-(2+1)d realization of the (1+1)d 3-4-5-0 lattice chiral fermion model with six-fermion interactions at one edge. We find gapless modes near the interacting edge for both weak and strong couplings, but the edge can be in a fully gapped SMG phase at intermediate coupling. We also identify spontaneous breaking of the model's $\mathbb{Z}_2$ symmetry above a critical interaction strength. Across all three boundary phases, we find quantized charge pumping with the same pumped charge per flux quantum. The spatial distribution of the pumped charge varies between phases. Besides charge pumping, we study how a single injected fermion propagates under open boundary conditions. In the SMG phase, an interaction-induced flavor-mixing current develops at the endpoints of the gapped edge, which is absent in the weak- and strong-coupling limits. This current reveals a charge-redistribution mechanism unique to the SMG phase. Additionally, we propose an analogy between charge pumping in this model and a topological leptogenesis scenario in the (3+1)d Standard Model. The anomaly-free chiral U(1) symmetries of the 3-4-5-0 model play a role analogous to the baryon-minus-lepton symmetry of the Standard Model. In both settings, charge pumping can be associated with a continuous deformation along a classically defined but quantum-anomalous direction, while a discrete subgroup remains an exact quantum symmetry.

papers.title_en: Hyperbolic scaling of the small-exponent limit in magnetic nonlinear electrodynamics
papers.abstract_en: A magnetic spacetime can approach Schwarzschild while its electromagnetic characteristics remain singular in the same parameter limit. We study this separation in fractional-power nonlinear electrodynamics as the exponent tends to zero with asymptotic mass, magnetic charge and nonlinear coupling independently fixed. The extraordinary polarization admits a common physical time direction only outside a boundary that grows as the inverse fourth root of the exponent. On this radial scale, the lapse tends to unity but the constitutive angular response retains a nondegenerate barrier and finite scaled critical data. An exact representation of the exterior electromagnetic energy yields complete second-order corrections to the orbit and impact, separating mass and charge contributions and their distinct cancellations. Constraining the mass to equal the electromagnetic self-energy preserves the leading critical constants while changing the approach from fourth-root to square-root corrections. Returning rays remain inside the admissible exterior and define a limiting scattering function with a calculated logarithmic strong-deflection coefficient. In the weak regime, constitutive bending decays as the inverse fourth power of scaled impact, whereas finite mass supplies a slower inverse-impact tail. We determine their competition scale, its accessibility above the critical impact, and the accuracy of the two-term approximation. Independent energy, orbit and scattering calculations check the expansions and resolve their parameter-dependent convergence. The analysis shows how a nearly vacuum background can support a distinct exterior optical limit through the nonlinear constitutive response.

papers.title_en: Nonlinear stability of Schwarzschild black holes for the Einstein-massless Dirac system in spherical symmetry
papers.abstract_en: In this paper, we establish the nonlinear stability of the Schwarzschild exterior for the spherically symmetric Einstein-massless Dirac system. More precisely, we consider sufficiently small perturbations of Schwarzschild characteristic initial data and prove that the corresponding maximal development remains globally controlled in the exterior region (orbital stability), and converges, in a suitable teleological double-null gauge, to a Schwarzschild spacetime with a final mass (asymptotic stability). In particular, the maximal future development contains a complete future null infinity and a regular event horizon, with a nonempty black hole region in its interior. The main difficulties in the proof arise from the delicate coupling between the Dirac operator and the geometry, compared with the scalar wave counterpart, as well as from the failure of the Dirac stress-energy tensor to satisfy a positive energy condition. To overcome these difficulties, we rely on a bootstrap argument coupling the geometry and the Dirac field. Working in suitable teleological double-null gauges adapted to the asymptotic null boundaries, we establish weighted energy estimates combining integrated local energy decay, red-shift estimates near the event horizon, and an rp-estimates towards null infinity. A core ingredient is the use of suitable reweightings of the spinor components, which allow us to close these estimates despite the nonlinear coupling to the geometry.

papers.title_en: Quantum Batteries in two-dimensional material-based Josephson Junctions
papers.abstract_en: We investigate the solid-state implementation of a Dicke-like quantum battery consisting of a two-dimensional material-based Josephson junction inductively coupled to a resonator, using graphene as a representative example. In this configuration, Andreev bound states naturally act as non-interacting, energetically non-degenerate two-level systems, and the setup allows for both single-photon and two-photon resonant processes. The coupling between the LC-circuit flux and the supercurrent through the junction gives rise to peculiar longitudinal interaction terms that have no counterpart in the conventional Dicke model. We demonstrate that these additional couplings can enhance energy storage for a proper range of parameters. The proposed architecture also enables an alternative, but comparable, charging protocol that relies on tuning the superconducting phase difference across the junction.

papers.title_en: Far-Zone Gravitational Interactions at the Sixth Post-Newtonian Order
papers.abstract_en: We compute the nonlinear far-zone dynamics of compact binaries at the sixth post-Newtonian (6PN) order in the effective field theory of general relativity. We derive the complete $\mathcal{O}(G^2)$ far-zone action of a generic multipolar source in both the causal and the conservative prescriptions. Besides the known tails and failed tails, it contains five new sectors generated by the nonlinear memory of the emitted waves. On scattering orbits, they contain a boundary term, nonlocal in time, fixed by the balance of angular momentum. The same construction yields the emitted waveforms, whose energy and angular-momentum fluxes balance the losses of the action. For the binary, the 6PN dynamics also requires PN corrections to the lower-order sectors, the iterated radiation reaction, and a coupling quadratic in the curvature of the composite source, whose coefficient we fix by matching the gravitational Compton amplitude to that of the constituents. We compute the two-radiation contributions to the total scattering angle at fourth, fifth and sixth post-Minkowskian (PM) order and to the conservative angle at 4PM and 5PM, retaining the integer-PN terms through 6PN. For the conservative angle, we give both the local and $γ$-3 prescriptions. Combined with the tail and the known potential contributions, our results reproduce the conservative and total 4PM angles and the second-self-force part of the conservative 5PM angle. Including the dissipative tail, we recover the total 5PM angle through 5PN and determine its new 6PN coefficient. At 6PM, the two-radiation contribution to the total angle extends the known 5PN result to 6PN.

papers.title_en: Tests of equivalence principle violation in doubly coupled dark energy
papers.abstract_en: Recent work has shown that a simple form of coupled dark energy with a constant coupling produces a good fit to the DESI data. In this scenario, dark matter, but not baryons, couples to a scalar field, thereby violating the weak equivalence principle (EP). We first generalize the coupled dark energy model by adding a nonminimal coupling between the scalar field and gravity, and dub the resulting model "doubly coupled dark energy". We then construct a parameter $E_P$ in this model that quantifies EP violation on cosmological scales and can be measured with large galaxy surveys in a model-independent way. Finally, we forecast constraints on the couplings for present and future spectroscopic galaxy surveys, namely DESI, Euclid, and SKA Phase 2 (SKA2). To keep the analysis as general as possible, we leave the initial power spectrum shape and the galaxy bias free to vary in several bins. Among these surveys, SKA2 could provide the tightest constraint on the coupling strength in the coupled dark energy scenario, with a relative $1σ$ uncertainty of $22\%$. The constraints weaken when both couplings are varied, but can be further improved by increasing the number of galaxies detected.

papers.title_en: A Charged Compact Star Solution for a Conducting Sphere
papers.abstract_en: This paper considers the simplest charged stellar model, namely, a uniform density star with electric charge distributed on its surface. In this model, we treat the uniform density star as a conducting sphere, where all electric charges are uniformly distributed on the surface and represented by a delta function. We obtain an analytical solution for the background metric of the star spacetime and find that the pressure of the perfect fluid inside the star is directed inward (negative pressure) near the inner surface. This is because the repulsive force between surface electric charges requires an inward pressure to maintain equilibrium. However, when the charge becomes too large, the pressure of the ideal fluid at the stellar center gets directed outwards again. This is because the electric field itself is also a part of the stress energy tensor $T_{μν}$, acting as a source of gravity. When the gravitational effect of the electric field dominates, the perfect fluid must provide outward pressure to balance the inward gravitational attraction. On the other hand, we have also studied the axial perturbation in charged spacetimes using the finite difference method. We found that axial Maxwell perturbation and axial gravitational perturbation are coupled in the star spacetime, making it difficult to separate the variables by coordinate transformation. The computational results show that the waveforms of quasinormal modes vary with different charges.

papers.title_en: Black Hole Dynamics at Fifth Post-Newtonian Order
papers.abstract_en: Using the worldline action in [2409.05860], we derive the total even-in-velocity (relative) impulse, scattering angle, and time delay at fifth post-Newtonian (5PN) order, including radiation-reaction and hereditary contributions at ${\cal O}(G^5ν^2)$ and ${\cal O}(G^6ν^2)$. We introduce an isotropic-like description which, together with the associated losses of energy and angular momentum, fixes the evolution of the system from scattering data. This framework opens the door to an unambiguous characterization of the underlying two-body dynamics solely in terms of scattering observables. Following [2409.05860], we isolate a conservative component using Feynman's $i0^+$ prescription. This sector contains both "tail-like" and "memory-like" contributions, the latter being nonlocal in time and described by a double Principal-Value integral. Owing to the local-in-time character of the corresponding (in-in) action, we establish a systematic procedure that is consistent with Feynman's prescription while preserving the complete local dynamics. This provides a universal contribution to the conservative (isotropic) Hamiltonian at 5PN order and, as a byproduct, also fixes the value of the Effective One Body coefficients $\{{\bar d}_{5{\rm loc}}, a_{6{\rm loc}}\}$ consistently with the Tutti-Frutti framework. For completeness, we analyse the "$γ\text{-}3$" prescription introduced in recent post-Minkowskian computations. When implemented in our formalism, we find exact agreement over the overlapping regime of validity. In contrast, Feynman's prescription yields a (local) memory-like contribution with the opposite sign at ${\cal O}(G^5ν^2)$. We also find that an analogous $γ\text{-}3$ rerouting at ${\cal O}(G^6ν^2)$ would be incompatible with the conjecture that all $π^2$ terms arise solely from the potential region, while Feynman's formulation preserves this expectation.

papers.title_en: Elastic boundaries in Stochastic Inflation
papers.abstract_en: In the context of stochastic inflation, specifying boundary conditions is often a requirement to distinguish domains where quantum diffusion takes place from regions where stochastic effects are suppressed compared to the standard slow-roll evolution. Yet, even though the transition between the two is expected to be smooth and continuous, most of the literature has hitherto focused on absorbing and reflective boundaries. We consider here the use of a broader class of boundaries, called elastic, which involves one free parameter interpolating between these two limiting cases. We show how the conventional stochastic-$δN$, and its recently proposed time-reversed counterpart adapt to such a class of boundary behaviour. As an illustration, we solve time-reversed stochastic inflation for an exactly flat semi-infinite potential with an elastic boundary, a setup where the standard stochastic-$δN$ formalism breaks down, and compare the results to the purely absorbing case. Quantitative differences are found in terms of skewness and tail behaviour. This suggests that the transition between stochastic inflation and subsequent evolution may have observable consequences. Finally, we show that an elastic boundary stands as an effective model for stochastic tunnelling through a Dirac delta potential barrier. This mechanism can be equivalently framed as a smooth transition of stochastic trajectories in a mirror virtual medium with specific absorption properties.

papers.title_en: An Infinite Family of Non-Rational VOAs from Strongly Coupled 4d Higgsless SCFTs
papers.abstract_en: We study an infinite family of strongly coupled four-dimensional $\mathcal N=2$ superconformal field theories (SCFTs) distinguished by a trivial Higgs branch, known as the $(A_2,D_{3m+1})$ Argyre-Douglas theories. We propose that their associated vertex operator algebras (VOAs) are the doublet algebras $\mathcal A(4m+2)$, an infinite family of non-rational vertex operator superalgebras with a remarkably simple strong generating set of only three fields. We provide several highly nontrivial checks of this proposal. In particular, we reproduce the four-dimensional conformal anomalies $a$ and $c$ from the VOA and analytically prove the exact equality between the Schur index of the SCFT and the supercharacter of the VOA. A key ingredient is a diagonal-gauging realization of the $(A_2,D_{3m+1})$ theories in terms of two simpler building blocks, which makes the Schur-index computation tractable. Remarkably, we find that the resulting Schur index of the $(A_2,D_{3m+1})$ theory coincides with that of $\mathcal N=4$ $SU(2)$ Super-Yang-Mills theory, up to an overall prefactor and an appropriate identification of fugacities. We also discuss a generalization to the two-parameter family $(A_{2s},D_{(2s+1)m+1})$, whose members likewise have trivial Higgs branches and admit diagonal-gauging realizations. A particularly interesting subfamily is $(A_{2s},D_{2s+2})$, for which the four-dimensional conformal anomalies coincide, $a=c$. As a byproduct, we also show that the doublet VOA $\mathcal A(4m+2)$ is not classically free for positive integer $m $, and we discuss its implications for the Schur and Macdonald indices. Our results reveal a systematic connection between Higgsless SCFTs, diagonal gauging, and strongly finite but non-rational vertex operator algebras.

papers.title_en: ZTF SNe Ia DR2: Towards cosmology-grade ZTF supernova light curves using scene modeling photometry
papers.abstract_en: The Zwicky Transient Facility (ZTF) is conducting a wide-field survey of the northern sky in three optical bands and the collaboration cosmology working group has released 3628 spectroscopically confirmed Type Ia supernovae (SNe Ia) discovered during its first 2.5 years of operation. This "ZTF SN Ia DR2" sample is the largest SN Ia dataset to date. Fully exploiting this dataset to improve understanding of the properties of dark energy requires a photometric accuracy of O(0.1%). This can be achieved using Scene Modeling Photometry (SMP), which is optimal to extract a transient signal (SN) from a complex background (its host), while ensuring a common flux estimator with nearby stars used as calibration reference. In this paper, we present the status of the SMP development and use it to assess the precision and accuracy of the ZTF SN Ia DR2 force photometry light curves. We reach a repeatability of the star observations better than 1%. However, we have identified a new sensor effect, dubbed "pocket-effect", which distorts the Point Spread Function (PSF) in a flux-dependent manner leading to non-linearities in the photometry of a few percent. Correcting for this effect requires time- and sensor-dependent corrections to be applied at the pixel level, which is currently under development. This effects affects all light curve releases to date -- both from forced photometry and scene modelling preventing ZTF SN Ia DR2 to be used for accurate cosmological inference. Comparing the SMP and forced photometry measurements, we find that stretch and color estimated from both processings are consistent, aside from a 10 mmag shift in color. This assess the robustness of results presented as part of the the ZTF SN Ia DR2 release. The absolute calibration however shifts by 90 mmag. A reprocessing of the full ZTF SN Ia DR2 dataset using the SMP method is currently in progress.

papers.title_en: The Devil Went Down to de Sitter: Divergent Effective Field Theory Expansions in Cosmology
papers.abstract_en: Effective field theories (EFTs) in de Sitter space, and in accelerating cosmologies more generally, must capture phenomena absent in flat space, most notably long-range correlations generated by spontaneous particle production. When heavy physics is integrated out in such time-dependent backgrounds, these effects leave an imprint on the EFT expansion: even at tree level, this is generically an asymptotic rather than convergent series. This is not a failure of EFT. The large-order behavior of the expansion coefficients encodes physical information inaccessible at any finite order, so cosmological EFTs contain hidden data. Using resurgence analysis, we show how this information can be systematically extracted to recover exact and non-perturbative predictions from the perturbative expansion. In the example we study, the resurgent completion is naturally organized in terms of the de Sitter $S$-matrix. This leads us to conjecture a prescription for extracting $S$-matrix data from cosmological EFTs in general. The framework extends to any setting where particle production, or a similar non-perturbative phenomenon, renders the EFT expansion asymptotic. A longer companion paper will provide a more detailed and pedagogical treatment.

papers.title_en: Bootstrapping a Higher-Derivative Cosmological Collider: Borel-Laplace Resummation and Stokes Phenomena
papers.abstract_en: We develop a higher-derivative cosmological bootstrap for massive spectators with quartic dispersion, $ω^2\propto k^4$, revealing a new boundary-value problem for inflationary correlators. The exchange equation becomes fourth order, and the collapsed limit becomes an irregular singular point, where collider and WKB branches coexist and exhibit Stokes phenomena. Since the folded configuration is now an ordinary point, the relativistic criterion of Bunch--Davies regularity at the folded singularity is no longer available. We instead impose an asymptotic boundary condition that removes the WKB branches and matches the surviving collider branches to Schwinger-Keldysh data. We also construct a convergent Borel-Laplace particular solution that resums a factorially divergent expansion and satisfies both bootstrap equations simultaneously; its leading collapsed-limit behavior is reproduced by direct in-in integrals. In the bispectrum, the squeezed-limit collider signal retains its mass-dependent frequency, while its amplitude and phase depend on the dispersion scale; near the equilateral configuration, the full shape is also sensitive to this scale and can change sign. Our results expose a new analytic structure of non-relativistic cosmological correlators and signatures beyond the squeezed limit.

papers.title_en: cWB-space: A time-frequency unmodelled transient-search pipeline for LISA
papers.abstract_en: The Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) will observe massive-black-hole mergers and other transient phenomena alongside many long-lived gravitational-wave signals. Some transients may be incompletely modeled or have waveforms that have not been anticipated. We present \texttt{cWB-space}, a pipeline that combines an unmodeled transient search, waveform reconstruction, and a time-frequency glitch classifier. The search identifies concentrations of signal power in time and frequency and reconstructs candidate waveforms without requiring a source template. The glitch classifier compares how candidates appear in different combinations of LISA's laser measurements, with the background estimated from the observed data. We test the pipeline with simulated black-hole binaries with aligned and precessing spins, burst signals with different shapes, and instrumental glitches. The response comparisons help assess a candidate's astrophysical or instrumental origin, while also revealing correlated glitches that can resemble gravitational waves. In the Sangria simulated LISA data, the search recovers all six injected massive-black-hole binaries as its six highest-ranked candidates. Their local reconstructions recover the main features of the injected waveforms over the intervals studied. These results demonstrate how an unmodeled search can connect transient identification with investigation of a candidate's origin and waveform recovery.

papers.title_en: Algorithmic Dualization of Unitary Circular Quivers
papers.abstract_en: We introduce a field-theoretic algorithm to find the $SL(2,\mathbb{Z})$ duality web of 3d $\mathcal{N}=4$ circular quiver theories with unitary gauge groups, extending the algorithm for linear quivers. Although circular and linear quivers share the same local structure, the circular topology requires additional ingredients, which we formulate in terms of topological and baryonic QFT blocks, together with new $SL(2,\mathbb{Z})$ duality moves acting on them. For good circular quivers, this provides a field-theoretic derivation of mirror symmetry and extends it to the full $SL(2,\mathbb{Z})$ duality web. We then study bad circular quivers, distinguishing between local badness, associated with under-balanced gauge nodes, and global badness, arising from the circular topology itself. In particular, we analyze the magnetic and electric dual frames of globally bad circular quivers and provide additional evidence for the proposed duality by matching the Higgs branch index with the dual Coulomb branch index. The latter exhibits a structure reminiscent of permutation-group gauging and reveals a refined relation to the ADHM quiver, flowing to the $\mathcal{N}=8$ infrared fixed point.

papers.title_en: Anomalies of TQFTs coupled to parameter spaces and constraints on ground-state degeneracies
papers.abstract_en: Anomalies of global symmetries can arise in long-range entangled quantum many-body systems and provide useful constraints on their dynamics. In this paper, we study anomalies of $d$-dimensional topological quantum field theories (TQFTs) coupled to parameter spaces and their implications for ground-state degeneracies. Specifically, we formulate anomalies as obstructions to constructing parametrized families of TQFTs. We discuss how the classification of these anomalies depends on the choice of topology on the universal $\mathrm{U}(1)$ $(d-1)$-form symmetry. In this framework, we use the projective ground-state bundle obtained by compactifying the TQFT on a spatial manifold to derive a general constraint relating its ground-state degeneracy $N$ to its torsion anomaly $ω$, expressed as $N\int_Wω\in\mathbb{Z}$ for bundles $W$ of spatial manifolds over closed surfaces. We apply this constraint to ground-state degeneracies of (2+1)-dimensional TQFTs with framing and 1-form symmetry anomalies and to obstructions to symmetry-preserving TQFTs. We also discuss implications for bordism generators and propose a conjecture on anomaly detection by manifolds fibered over surfaces.

papers.title_en: Solvable coupled cluster states in $d=\infty$ with prescribed momentum distribution
papers.abstract_en: Two of the most successful ideas in many-body theory, the exponential coupled cluster ansatz and DMFT, have to date developed separately. We establish a connection between them, by showing that the infinite dimensional limit of the hypercubic lattice allows the exact closed-form evaluation of static expectation values of coupled cluster wave functions, provided the cluster amplitudes admit a low-rank decomposition. As a result, evaluation errors -- a serious concern in conventional coupled cluster theory -- can be disentangled from limitations to expressivity of coupled cluster states. For this family of coupled cluster states, the cavity construction in $d\to\infty$ exactly reduces the environment of a lattice site to a Gaussian Grassmann kernel, and irreducible diagrams for one-body expectation values are found to be site-diagonal (in analogy to the DMFT self-energy). The resulting ``impurity problem" is an integral over a finite number of Grassmann variables rather than a dynamical quantum impurity problem, so that static observables derive exactly from a static self-consistency condition: a wave function counterpart of DMFT. For the simplest case of a cluster amplitude restricted to rank-one doubles, we obtain the momentum distribution in closed form. We show that any momentum distribution can be realized by a state that is the exact and unique ground state of an explicit parent Hamiltonian with a gapless single-particle tunnelling spectrum. By construction these coupled cluster states variationally recover low order perturbation theory for the Hubbard model. Their failure in the strong coupling regime near the Mott transition diagnoses a fundamental limitation of coupled cluster doubles. Intriguingly, our family of coupled cluster wave functions includes a gapless state with zero quasiparticle weight, with a momentum distribution that is completely smooth at the Fermi energy.

papers.title_en: Scattering of massless scalar waves by higher-dimensional regular black holes in general relativity coupled to nonlinear electrodynamics
papers.abstract_en: We study the scattering of planar massless scalar waves by the family of higher-dimensional regular black holes in general relativity coupled to nonlinear electrodynamics, which unifies the Bardeen and Hayward models in any dimension. The scalar field is a neutral test field that propagates in the bulk, and in the geometric-optics limit, its rays are the null geodesics of the spacetime, so that the unstable circular null geodesics of the background geometry control the scattering. We combine the classical scattering of null geodesics, the glory approximation, which we generalize to $D$ dimensions, and the partial-wave analysis in $D=5,6,7$. We show that at a fixed frequency, the wave cross section diverges in the forward direction as $θ^{-4}$ in any dimension, with a coefficient fixed by the mass, while the steeper classical law $θ^{-(D-2)^{2}/(D-3)}$ appears only at larger angles and higher frequencies. The charge parameter decreases the critical and the glory impact parameters and widens the glory fringes, and in higher dimensions, the glory pattern has fewer and wider fringes and a weaker backward intensity. For the matched configurations studied here, backward intensity and low-frequency absorption provide the clearest differences, while the intermediate-to-high-frequency spectra are close.

papers.title_en: Running cosmological constant in light of recent CMB-BAO data
papers.abstract_en: We revisit single-field slow-roll inflation driven by a running cosmological constant, i.e. a cosmological constant receiving a logarithmic radiative correction, in light of the latest CMB-BAO data. The relative radiative correction $δ$ is treated as a free parameter of the model and allowed to be positive or negative. For positive $δ$, the predictions interpolate between a logarithmic regime and a linear inflation one. Compatibility with CMB-only data is confined to a narrow stripe near the $2σ$ border where $δ$ is relatively large. On the other hand, the predictions fit easily within the constraints including BAO data in a wide range of parameters. For negative $δ$, the slow-roll approximation breaks down at small field values and the predictions are excluded by data. However, once the effective mass contribution inside the logarithmic correction is taken into account, the negative $δ$ potential develops a local maximum and behaves like a hilltop model, achieving compatibility with CMB-only data, while agreement with CMB-BAO data is possible only at $2σ$.

papers.title_en: No generalised contextuality from the vacuum
papers.abstract_en: We show that, under certain conditions, generalised contextuality, in the sense introduced by Spekkens, cannot be created from the vacuum of a quantum field. Initial noncontextual qudit states do not become contextual just by interacting with a quantum field. This is verified in two scenarios. First, in a perturbative approach where the time evolution operator is expanded in powers of the coupling constant. Second, in the limit of zero energy gap in the spectrum of the free detector Hamiltonian. Our results are at the opposite side of what has been recently obtained in the literature regarding the harvesting of Kochen-Specker contextuality. Our results demonstrate that the existing notions of contextuality can be independent of one another and that contextuality harvesting depends on which precise notion is used.

papers.title_en: Neutrino Oscillation in a Static Dihole Geometry
papers.abstract_en: We investigate neutrino flavor oscillations in the static equal-mass Majumdar-Papapetrou dihole geometry, restricting the propagation to the symmetry plane. Within the null approximation, we derive the leading contribution to the neutrino phase and numerically evaluate the geodesic integrals. For two neutrino flavors, interference between different trajectories introduces a dependence on the individual neutrino masses and on the neutrino mass ordering for nonmaximal mixing. We analyze the transition probability in different spacetime configurations possessing two light rings, a merged light ring (critical configuration), and no light rings in the equatorial plane. In the weak-lensing regime, the transition probability generally increases with the black holes' individual masses, while variations in the half-separation produce no qualitative change in the transition probability. In stronger-lensing configurations, variations in both the mass and half-separation modify the heights and positions of the extrema, with no monotonic increase or decrease in the transition probability. For the critical and no-light-ring configurations studied, we identify three zero-winding trajectories connecting the source and detector, including one passing near the symmetry axis. The probability remains oscillatory, and its oscillatory pattern depends strongly on the neutrino energy.

papers.title_en: Topological Multi-Natural Inflation
papers.abstract_en: We investigate topological inflation in minimal multi-natural inflation, in which the axion potential consists of two cosine terms. Focusing on the high-scale regime, we perform a systematic parameter scan for representative ratios of the two periods and identify regions consistent with current constraints on the scalar spectral index and tensor-to-scalar ratio, including those from the Atacama Cosmology Telescope. The interplay of the two harmonics allows departures from the quartic hilltop limit and accommodates the higher spectral index favored by recent cosmological data combinations. We characterize the hilltop and near-inflection-point branches and analyze the associated vacuum structure and domain-wall properties. We also discuss a symmetry-breaking origin of the required domain walls when the inflaton is the angular component of a complex scalar field. We identify regions in which the observational constraints and the adopted criteria for topological inflation are simultaneously satisfied, including regions with a sub-Planckian axion decay constant. Our results show that the observational tension encountered in the minimal quartic double-well model need not extend to topological inflation in a minimal multi-natural axion potential.

papers.title_en: Formation of Micron-sized Presolar Graphite Grains in Low-energy Supernova Ejecta
papers.abstract_en: Presolar graphite grains with supernova isotopic signatures provide direct evidence that large graphite grains formed in supernova ejecta. However, theoretical calculations of dust formation in supernovae have typically predicted graphite grains smaller than $0.1\,{\rm μm}$, leaving unclear the physical conditions required to form those grains with radii of order $1\,{\rm μm}$. We systematically investigate graphite nucleation and growth in expanding supernova ejecta by varying the explosion energy, ejecta mass, initial ejecta radius, and ejected $^{56}$Ni mass. We use a simplified one-zone model that follows the temperature and density evolution including adiabatic cooling, radiative cooling, and heating by radioactive nickel. We show that the final graphite grain size is mainly determined by the product of the mass density of atomic carbon available for grain growth and the local cooling timescale, both evaluated at a reference temperature of $2000\,{\rm K}$. Our models show that graphite growth is favored by lower explosion energy, larger ejecta mass, and smaller initial ejecta radius, which keep the gas denser near the graphite-condensation temperature. When radioactive heating and radiative cooling are included, explosions with $E_{\rm exp}\sim10^{50}\,{\rm erg}$ and $M_{\rm Ni}\lesssim10^{-3}\,M_\odot$ can form $1$-$10\,μ{\rm m}$ graphite grains in the ejected helium layer or carbon-oxygen core, whereas $E_{\rm exp}\sim10^{51}\,{\rm erg}$ models do not. These results suggest that micron-sized presolar supernova graphite preferentially forms in faint-supernova-like explosions with low explosion energies, little ejected nickel, and helium layer or carbon-oxygen core ejecta.

papers.title_en: Cosmology with post-EoR 21 cm Intensity Mapping surveys: power spectrum measurements in the last decade
papers.abstract_en: The technique of 21 cm intensity mapping (IM) is emerging as a possible, cost-effective method to supplement optical surveys to map the large-scale structure, and extend their redshift reach, with projects aiming to cover a large range of post-EoR redshifts, from z=0 to z=6. Since the early discussions 20 years ago, a few dedicated interferometers have been built, and surveys have been carried out using them as well as general purpose radio instruments. An introduction to late-time cosmology with 21 cm intensity mapping is given, highlighting the main scientific and technical challenges. We present then an overview of different instrument concepts and survey strategies, followed by a discussion of outstanding data analysis challenges, most notably the foreground subtraction, which is a major issue in IM. We carry on with a presentation of the currently active projects and the 21 cm signal measurements which have been obtained, either in cross-correlation with optical surveys, or as the autocorrelation power spectrum. Finally, we discuss briefly the prospects for this field with future instruments and surveys such as SKA, HIRAX and CHORD.

papers.title_en: Lifting the mixed to the pure: quantum phases of matter from canonical purification
papers.abstract_en: Pure-state quantum phases are defined through finite-depth local unitary connections. This concept of phases has recently been generalized to mixed states in terms of locally reversible channels. In this work, we establish a fundamental relation between mixed-state phases and pure-state phases. We show that a locally reversible channel between mixed states can be lifted to a local isometry between their canonical purifications; thus, if two mixed states are in the same phase, then their canonical purifications are in the same pure-state phase. Furthermore, an explicit construction of the lifting isometry is given by ``half'' of the Petz recovery map, suggesting that the Petz recovery map \emph{without rotation} is enough to connect mixed state phases. We illustrate our results with two examples: toric code under bit flip noise and Chern insulator under fermion number noise.

papers.title_en: Finite-Depth Null Capture and Mass-History Sensitivity in Vaidya Spacetime
papers.abstract_en: We formulate a finite-depth endpoint map for past-directed null rays in dynamical black-hole spacetimes, retaining an unresolved label when no terminal is reached before a prescribed optical depth. For regular transverse terminal hits, common-flow, transversality, and separation hypotheses make the regular decision sets open and the endpoint label locally constant. In Schwarzschild spacetime, the resulting finite-depth capture circle converges to the standard critical circle as $\exp[-L/(3M)]$ when the cutoff is measured in static-observer optical depth. We then apply the construction to ingoing Vaidya spacetime. Two $C^4$ accretion profiles that coincide on a neighborhood of the observation event, and therefore have identical local mass and metric jets there, nevertheless produce distinct finite-depth critical angles. For the baseline protocol, $Δ_{\mathrm{hist}}α_{45}=0.0819062ε-0.0231767ε^2+O(ε^3)$. A backward adjoint gives an explicit causal kernel representing the first-order response to the mass history. The kernel is broad, peaks away from the photon-sphere dwell region, and changes between finite backgrounds even where their instantaneous masses agree. The quadratic coefficient is independently confirmed by centered nonlinear solutions and Richardson extrapolation. These results separate instability-controlled cutoff convergence from globally transported mass-history sensitivity.

papers.title_en: Large-Level Limit of Doubled Chern-Simons Theory Part I: Regular Sector, Boundaries and Interfaces
papers.abstract_en: We study three-dimensional $BF$ theory as the large-level limit of the doubled Chern-Simons theory $G_k\times G_{-k}$ for simply connected, compact, simple $G$, a limit that connects the symmetry topological field theories of finite and continuous symmetries. Lines whose two highest weights grow linearly with $k$ at fixed difference become $BF$ lines, with magnetic flux set by their average and electric charge equal to their difference. Representing level-$k$ torus states as normalized flux-charge wave packets, we prove that every fixed modular transformation of any fixed normalizable state with regular flux converges in the strong-$*$ topology to its $BF$ counterpart. The Dehn twist gives each line exactly its Aharonov-Bohm phase at every level, while $S$ converges to a Fourier transform exchanging flux and charge, without escaping to singular holonomies or large charges. States that approach singular fluxes at large $k$ are not covered. The natural boundary 2d theory is speculated to be a decompactified boson in the abelian case $G=U(1)$, and $\dim G$ non-compact free scalars for general $G$. For $SU(2)$, we discuss the gapped interfaces between adjacent levels, which must shift some flux or charge by a finite amount. In the $k\rightarrow\infty$ limit the interface is conjectured to be the $c=1$ Runkel-Watts theory.

papers.title_en: Andreev-Enhanced Conductance in a Bilayer Graphene Quantum Point Contact
papers.abstract_en: Quantum point contacts provide a platform for probing mode-dependent Andreev reflection. Here, we demonstrate Andreev-enhanced conductance in a gate-defined bilayer graphene quantum point contact coupled to a superconducting aluminum electrode. Electrostatic gating enables sequential mode occupation, verified by normal-state conductance quantization. In the superconducting state, the conductance is enhanced within the conductance plateaus, while the enhancement decreases between plateaus, consistent with the nonlinear transmission dependence of Andreev reflection. The enhancement yields effective transmission probabilities up to 0.9, and extends over a bias window of approximately 140 $μ$V, which we associate with a proximity-induced superconducting gap, close to the gap of the aluminum film. For in-plane fields, the enhancement persists up to the critical field, and the bias window follows the spectral gap predicted by Abrikosov-Gor'kov theory. In contrast, perpendicular fields suppress the enhancement approximately linearly from zero field, deviating from homogeneous pair breaking and indicative of flux penetration.

papers.title_en: Two-loop matter power spectrum from FFTLog and kite integrals
papers.abstract_en: We present a fast and accurate method for computing the two-loop matter power spectrum in the Effective Field Theory of Large-Scale Structure (EFTofLSS). Using FFTLog, we decompose the linear power spectrum into complex power laws, reducing the two-loop corrections to cosmology-independent massless Feynman integrals of kite topology. A central numerical challenge is the evaluation of these integrals for complex powers with large imaginary parts, where the highly oscillatory integrands make accurate numerical evaluation particularly challenging. We overcome this difficulty using a Mellin--Barnes representation summed over a uniform lattice, achieving approximately ten digit precision even for large imaginary powers, with an error estimate for each integral. The resulting precomputed matrices allow the two-loop power spectrum to be evaluated for a new cosmology in a few milliseconds. Comparing with direct numerical integration, we find agreement at the $10^{-4}$ level relative to the power spectrum up to $k=0.2$ $h$Mpc$^{-1}$ after accounting for EFTofLSS counterterm contributions and FFTLog decomposition errors. The same framework extends to biased tracers and redshift-space distortions, providing the building blocks for general two-loop calculations in EFTofLSS. We make the code for evaluating the kite integrals publicly available, together with precomputed matrices and an implementation for the two-loop matter power spectrum as a concrete application. Our results can be directly incorporated into existing FFTLog-based codes for large-scale structure, extending their current one-loop capabilities to two loops within the same computational framework.

papers.title_en: Boundary preparation of strong Mpemba states in holography
papers.abstract_en: We study the boundary preparation of strong Mpemba states in a probe Abelian Higgs model on a fixed AdS black brane. Different drives ending at the same charge density can prepare states with different slow mode amplitudes and relaxation behavior. Two pulses cancel the slowest mode at linear order, but charge exchange during preparation and radial Maxwell feedback regenerate the slow tail at cubic order. We derive the complete cubic correction from the lower order field equations, including feedback after source removal, and use it to predict a compensating pulse. Full nonlinear evolution confirms that cubic compensation reduces the residual slow amplitude from $O(ε^3)$ to $O(ε^5)$. For a representative protocol at final density $ρ_f=3$ and $ε=0.05$, cubic compensation suppresses the slow amplitude by a factor of about $600$ relative to the linear prescription. Cubic compensation extends the period of fast relaxation without changing the final quasinormal mode spectrum. Further nonlinear tuning suppresses the residual slow amplitude to the level of numerical resolution. The excess free energy of the prepared states can exceed that of a weakly driven reference at release and fall below it during subsequent relaxation. Three pulses also suppress a second slow channel over the resolved time window and reveal interference between faster modes. Starting from a common initial state, controls with zero net charge transfer reach a given relaxation threshold sooner than passive relaxation, even when the full control duration is included.

papers.title_en: On the Geroch conjecture for toric gravitational instantons
papers.abstract_en: Geroch conjectured that the local solutions of the vacuum Einstein equations with two commuting Killing fields and vanishing twist constants are generated from flat space by an infinite-dimensional group of transformations, and Hauser and Ernst proved this for stationary axisymmetric spacetimes near the axis. The solutions generated from flat space by the transformations with finitely many poles in the spectral parameter are the solitons of Belinski and Zakharov. We prove a solitonic form of the conjecture in Riemannian signature, for toric gravitational instantons. The proof combines Weinstein's uniqueness argument, a closed formula for the soliton metrics in Hankel determinants and a degree argument. It also applies to the toric Ricci-flat metrics with conical singularities constructed by Li and Sun.

papers.title_en: The twistor construction of toric gravitational instantons
papers.abstract_en: We give an explicit construction of all ALF and ALE toric gravitational instantons in terms of certain rational matrix functions of one complex variable on the Riemann sphere; these provide patching matrices for their corresponding twistor holomorphic vector bundles. The reconstruction of the instantons arises from the solution to a Riemann--Hilbert splitting problem and we show how this can be solved via linear algebra, resembling but not equivalent to the Belinski--Zakharov ansatz. This construction gives a complete classification together with an explicit form for all toric gravitational instantons up to the resolutions of conical and orbifold singularities. We illustrate the formalism by computer--assisted numerical construction of two new ALF (but not AF) gravitational instantons with five nodes.

papers.title_en: Nucleon Wave Functions from QCD Vacuum Topology
papers.abstract_en: Instantons, as topologically nontrivial gauge field configurations, provide a microscopic mechanism for chiral symmetry breaking and the $U_A(1)$ anomaly in QCD. Within the instanton liquid model (ILM), instantons generate multi-fermion interactions governed by their density and size. Using this framework, we develop a microscopic description of the nucleon based on instanton-induced quark--quark correlations. We derive the diquark interaction kernels arising from single instantons and instanton--anti-instanton molecules, revealing a strong attraction in the scalar channel and weaker correlations in the spin-one channels. Embedding these interactions in a covariant, permutation-symmetric Bethe--Salpeter--Faddeev equation yields a nucleon mass $m_N=939.53~{\rm MeV}$, with a predominantly scalar-diquark component ($98\%$) and a small axial-vector admixture ($2\%$) around the mass pole. Despite its small weight, the small admixture generates substantial spin--isospin interference, yielding an axial charge $g_A=1.265$, close to experiment. The resulting covariant amplitude is analytically continued to the light front to obtain the leading three-quark wave function. The corresponding unpolarized, helicity, and transversity parton distributions, along with their QCD-evolved moments, provide a direct connection to lattice QCD calculations and global-fit analyses. Our results show that the topology of the QCD vacuum organizes not only the nucleon mass and spin structure, but also its leading valence partonic content, providing a microscopic foundation for a more complete description including confinement and higher Fock components.

papers.title_en: A multi-wavelength view of PSR J0437-4715 with NICER and other missions: Radius measurements from far-ultraviolet to hard X-ray pulse profile modeling
papers.abstract_en: We report updated mass and radius measurements for the millisecond pulsar PSR J0437-4715 obtained with pulse profile modeling of the emission from the far-ultraviolet to the hard X-rays. Using an extended 2.56 Ms Neutron Star Interior Composition ExploreR (NICER) dataset together with XMM-Newton, Nuclear Spectroscopic Telescope ARray and Hubble Space Telescope observations, we perform Bayesian inference with models describing the thermal emission from hot spots of increasing complexities, together with the rest of the warm NS surface, as well as the non-thermal emission component represented by a phase-dependent (pulsed) power-law. With this comprehensive model and broadband data set, as well as radio timing priors on the mass, distance and inclination, our headline result for PSR J0437-4715 led to a mass M = 1.377(-0.034)(+0.038) Msun and an equatorial radius Req = 11.35(-0.39)(+0.40) km, one of the narrowest measurements of Req from NICER observations of millisecond pulsars. The geometric configuration favors a non-antipodal hot spot distribution, as noted in previous analyses of this pulsar. When combined with recent measurements of M and Req of other pulsars, the tight constraints from PSR J0437-4715 further reduce the allowed range of the dense matter equation of state, excluding those that predict radii above 12.0 km (at the 68% level) for all NS masses.

papers.title_en: Sterile neutrino dark matter in conformal Majoron models
papers.abstract_en: We study sterile neutrino dark matter (DM) in a classically conformal U(1)' extension of the Standard Model with three right-handed neutrinos and a Majoron-like singlet scalar that generate the observed pattern of active neutrino masses and mixing via the type-I seesaw mechanism. Working in the regime of strongly suppressed active-sterile mixing, we show that the observed DM abundance can be produced through freeze-in from feeble interactions mediated by the heavy Z' and the conformal scalar. We solve the Boltzmann equation for the nonthermal phase-space distribution and confront the scenario with Lyman-$α$ and strong gravitational lensing data by computing the matter power spectrum. For keV-mass sterile neutrinos we identify the viable parameter space consistent with the inferred relic density and structure-formation and X-ray bounds, including regions compatible with a tentative 3.5 keV line. If a second sterile state is long-lived, late decays can realize a two-component setup that alleviates the $S_8$ tension. However, explanations of the 3.5 keV line and the $S_8$ tension are incompatible with the strong-lensing limit from JWST if the neutrinos saturate the relic abundance. In a highly fine-tuned variant of the model, the 220 PeV KM3NeT event can also be explained by invoking the decay of a superheavy sterile neutrino.

papers.title_en: Superconductivity in doped spin multimer systems
papers.abstract_en: Binding energy, which quantifies pair formation, is a key factor in the emergence of superconductivity. Here, we show that even when multiple spins are complexly coupled, hole-doped systems can be mapped, in the strong-binding-energy limit, onto an effective hardcore boson model equivalent to the XXZ model, and exhibit promising signatures of superconductivity. We demonstrate this theory analytically and numerically in the double Kondo lattice model. Using the density-matrix renormalization group method, we show that a pairing state is maintained via a crossover even for parameters away from the strong-coupling regime. Additionally, we find that once binding energies are sufficiently generated, pair correlations develop similarly regardless of the details of local spin correlations. Our findings provide useful insights into the mechanism of superconductivity.

papers.title_en: Creating functional nanostructures for vortex manipulation in superconducting Bi$_\text{2}$Sr$_\text{2}$CaCu$_\text{2}$O$_\text{8+x}$ thin films via focused He ion beam irradiation
papers.abstract_en: Bi$_2$Sr$_2$CaCu$_2$O$_{8+x}$ (Bi-2212) is a highly anisotropic high-temperature superconductor exhibiting unique vortex dynamics due to its layered structure. Precise nanoscale patterning of ultrathin Bi-2212 films remains challenging, limiting controlled studies of vortex pinning. Here, we employ 30 keV focused helium ion beam (He-FIB) irradiation to fabricate periodic arrays of columnar defects with 100 nm spacings in optimally-doped Bi-2212 thin films, thereby creating artificial vortex pinning centers. Magnetotransport measurements reveal pronounced vortex matching effects, evidenced by minima in magnetoresistance and peaks in critical current at commensurate magnetic fields. The angular dependence of magnetoresistance and critical current scale with an effective magnetic field, indicating strong confinement of pancake vortices along irradiation-induced tracks. These findings demonstrate the efficacy of He-FIB nanopatterning in modulating the superconducting properties in Bi-2212 thin films, providing a platform for fundamental studies of vortex matter and advancing prospects for device applications based on this highly anisotropic superconductor.

papers.title_en: Black hole thermodynamics at null infinity. Part 2: Open systems, Markovian dynamics and work extraction from non-rotating black holes
papers.abstract_en: Black hole thermodynamics provides a unique setting in which general relativity, quantum field theory, and statistical mechanics converge. In semiclassical gravity, this interplay culminates in the generalized second law (GSL), whose modern proofs rely on information theoretic techniques applied to algebras of observables defined on null hypersurfaces. These proofs exhibit close structural parallels with the thermodynamics of open quantum systems governed by Markovian dynamics. In this work, we draw parallels between the dynamics of quantum fields in regions bounded by non expanding causal horizons and the thermodynamics of quantum systems weakly coupled to equilibrium reservoirs. We introduce a dictionary relating late time boundary conditions to the choice of reservoir, vacuum states to fixed points of the dynamics, and modular Hamiltonians to thermodynamic potentials. Building on results from a companion paper on dual generalized second laws at future null infinity, we show that additional terms appearing in the associated thermodynamic potentials admit a natural interpretation as work contributions. We demonstrate that certain non thermal vacuum states at null infinity allow for the operation of autonomous thermal engines and enable work extraction from the radiation. Extending the analysis to the Unruh vacuum in Schwarzschild and Kerr backgrounds, we obtain generalized grand potential type laws incorporating grey body effects and angular momentum fluxes. Altogether, our results clarify the thermodynamic description of black hole dynamics and place it within the broader framework of open quantum thermodynamics.

papers.title_en: Primordial black holes and gravitational waves from aligned axion inflation
papers.abstract_en: We study the production of primordial black holes (PBHs) and scalar-induced gravitational waves (SIGWs) in aligned axion inflation through the transition between two stages of inflation. The first stage proceeds along a metastable trajectory and ends when this trajectory loses stability, causing the fields to turn towards the attractor of the second inflationary stage. During the transition, coupled adiabatic--entropy evolution produces a localized enhancement of the curvature power spectrum. We compute the PBH abundance from this spectrum assuming Gaussian primordial curvature perturbations and using the nonlinear compaction-function formalism with a spectrum-dependent collapse threshold and critical collapse. Representative benchmark solutions yield asteroid-mass PBHs with a potentially significant dark-matter abundance, together with an associated SIGW background.

papers.title_en: Black hole thermodynamics at null infinity. Part 1: Dual Generalized Second Law
papers.abstract_en: The generalized second law (GSL) of black hole thermodynamics asserts the monotonic increase of the generalized entropy combining the black hole area and the entropy of quantum fields outside the horizon. Modern proofs of the GSL rely on information theoretic methods and are typically formulated using algebras of observables defined on the event horizon together with a vacuum state invariant under horizon symmetries, inducing a geometric modular flow. In this work, we formulate a dual version of the generalized second law from the perspective of asymptotic observers at future null infinity, who do not have access to the black hole area. Our approach exploits the dependence of the second law on the choice of algebra of observables and of a reference state invariant under suitable symmetries, in close analogy with open quantum thermodynamics. Using algebraic quantum field theory and modular theory, we analyze several physically motivated vacuum states, including the Hartle Hawking state and two classes of regularized vacua. We show that, at null infinity, the monotonic quantity governing an irreversible evolution is no longer the generalized entropy, but rather a thermodynamic potential constructed from asymptotic observables.
