Depending on the chosen vacuum, this potential takes the form of the free energy or of a generalized grand potential built from the Bondi mass and additional (angular) mode dependent chemical potentials. The resulting inequalities define a dual generalized second law at future null infinity, which can be consistently combined with the standard GSL involving variations of the black hole area.

papers.title_en: Non-Clifford quantum cellular automata from invertible topological quantum field theories
papers.abstract_en: Quantum cellular automata (QCAs) describe locality-preserving quantum dynamics and link quantum information, many-body physics, and topological quantum field theory (TQFT). Constructing a QCA from a TQFT, however, remains challenging: although a topological action yields a Hamiltonian with commuting terms that realizes the desired ground state, it does not by itself specify an automorphism of the full operator algebra. We develop a unified algebraic construction that extends such Hamiltonians to complete separator-flipper algebras on the full tensor-product Hilbert space, thereby defining the corresponding QCAs microscopically. In 3 spatial dimensions, our framework unifies all previously known QCA constructions associated with the $\mathbb{Z}_8\times\mathbb{Z}_2$ subgroup of the Witt group, including the $U(1)_2$ and $U(1)_4$ QCAs. The same algebraic structure yields new infinite families of generalized $U(1)_2$ and $U(1)_4$ non-Clifford QCAs in spatial dimensions $d=4k-1$. We also reformulate the 4-dimensional $w_2w_3$ QCA and use it to construct QCAs from TQFTs associated with arbitrary products of Stiefel--Whitney classes. For example, we explicitly construct two infinite families: $w_2^nw_3^m$ QCAs in dimension $d=2n+3m-1$ and $w_2w_{4k-1}$ QCAs in dimension $d=4k$. For the 5-dimensional $w_3^2$ and $w_2^3$ QCAs, our construction gives finite-depth quantum circuits, consistent with the cobordism classification. More generally, we show that our construction yields a finite-depth quantum circuit whenever the corresponding Stiefel-Whitney number vanishes on every closed oriented manifold. Overall, these results convert invertible TQFTs into microscopic QCAs, provide higher-dimensional constructions beyond the Clifford setting, and open a systematic route to characterizing their stable structures and boundary anomalies.

papers.title_en: $T\overline{T}$ correlators from tensionless strings
papers.abstract_en: Motivated by earlier approaches, we develop a worldsheet framework for computing correlation functions in the single trace $T \overline{T}$-deformed tensionless AdS$_3$/CFT$_2$ duality. By describing the deformed bulk theory as a Berkovits-Vafa $\mathcal{N}=4$ topological string, we obtain a consistent definition of physical states and correlation functions, yielding a tractable setup for testing aspects of holography beyond AdS/CFT. We construct deformed physical vertex operators and compute their tree-level two-point functions exactly. We discuss the relation of our results to previous proposals for $T \overline{T}$-deformed two-point functions obtained from alternative worldsheet approaches, JT gravity, and perturbative field theory computations.

papers.title_en: Unitarity Methods for Magnus Amplitudes
papers.abstract_en: Magnus amplitudes refer to the matrix elements of the logarithm of the $S$-matrix. Modern unitarity methods construct cut-constructible parts of scattering amplitudes without directly invoking Feynman diagrams, offering an efficient way of obtaining loop integrands for scattering amplitudes. A procedure is proposed that adapts unitarity methods to the computation of Magnus amplitudes by modifying the $i0^+$ prescriptions of scattering amplitude integrands. A sufficient condition for applying the procedure at the level of master integrals is identified.

papers.title_en: Double diffraction production for dipole-dipole scattering at high energies
papers.abstract_en: This paper is a first attempt to describe double diffractive production in dipole-dipole scattering within high energy QCD. Our approach is based on summing large BFKL Pomeron loops, which generate two clusters of hadrons separated by a rapidity gap. Unlike in the BK framework, our approach allows both clusters to carry large masses. We derive the cross section for the production of two such clusters and show that it exhibits geometric scaling. Testing this scaling behaviour against data from high-energy colliders such as the LHC will be a crucial step in establishing whether large Pomeron loops play a major role in high energy QCD dynamics, and in particular in the unitarization of the scattering amplitude.

papers.title_en: The Dynamical Mass Profiles of Galaxy Groups - Application to IllustrisTNG-300
papers.abstract_en: We present a new rescaling and stacking method to test cold dark matter predictions through the dynamical modelling of galaxy groups using the Jeans equation. We test the viability of this method on idealised, line-of-sight group data at $z=0$ in the IllustrisTNG-300 simulation, using subhalos and satellite galaxies as tracers. Dynamical mass profiles are measured using the code `Gravsphere' for seven distinct quality cuts, three on the dark matter substructure and four on the `visible' satellite galaxies. When using the dark matter substructure, we find that selecting subhalos by their infall time onto the group provides the best recovery of the true mass profile. When using satellite galaxies we instead find that selecting quenched satellites provides the best recovery. In both cases the mass profile is recovered within $<1σ$ of the true value up to $\sim 1.5$ times the median host virial radius. However, we also find the recovered velocity anisotropy to be biased towards negative values for all seven of our subhalo samples beyond the median host virial radius. This suggests dynamical systematics may still be present in the data, which will need to be quantified in future work before application to surveys.

papers.title_en: From thermogravity to thermocosmology with a running non-conservation scale
papers.abstract_en: Thermogravity offers a novel approach to cosmic acceleration, deriving trace-free gravitational equations and matter non-conservation from thermodynamic processes in spacetime. We extend this framework towards thermocosmology by introducing a running non-conservation scale $L_2(H)$, while restricting non-conservation to cold dark matter. We investigate two prescriptions, namely a Hubble-proportional rate and an inverse-Hubble running model, deriving their cosmological dynamics and effective geometric dark-energy description. The first admits an exact analytical solution and is related to quadratic running-vacuum cosmologies, while the second approaches standard matter dilution at early times and allows reversals in the direction of energy exchange. Interestingly, the reconstructed geometric dark energy can exhibit quintessence-like and phantom-like behavior, including smooth crossings of the phantom divide, without introducing a phantom field or superacceleration. A unified dynamical-system analysis reveals distinct matter-era critical configurations and a continuous family of de Sitter solutions that are transversely attracting under suitable conditions. Confronting both models with Pantheon+ Type Ia supernovae, cosmic chronometers, and DESI DR2 baryon acoustic oscillations, we find a mild preference for positive present-day matter non-conservation. The Akaike information criterion slightly favors the thermogravity scenarios, whereas the Bayesian information criterion favors the simpler $Λ$CDM model. Thus, running thermocosmology provides a viable framework for nontrivial effective dark-energy dynamics.

papers.title_en: Homogeneous Spectral Freedom and Hadamard Consistency of Perturbative Green Functions
papers.abstract_en: Perturbative mode equations often admit formally different particular solutions whose spectral sums appear to have different short-distance singularities. We formulate a general diagnostic which separates this representational freedom from a genuine change of quantum state: for a fixed normally hyperbolic operator, two Hadamard two-point functions can differ only by a smooth homogeneous bisolution. Thus, a nonsmooth term generated by rearranging a perturbative source must be traced either to a changed operator or to inadmissible homogeneous spectral data. We apply the criterion to two impulsive plane-wave backgrounds. Starting directly from the metrics, we recompute the wave operators, modes, world functions, and Van Vleck determinants. Exact-mode matching and the geometrical construction agree through second order for the first profile. In the second, correcting the metric changes the leading perturbation from quadratic to linear order in the wave parameter and eliminates inverse transverse-momentum poles, while the corrected metric retains an exact aligned null-radiation Einstein source. In both examples the singular Green function is precisely the perturbative expansion of the Hadamard parametrix; the additional logarithms arise from momentum-singular homogeneous data. For the exactly soluble first profile, the standard flat-normalized plane-wave prescription gives a vanishing renormalized stress tensor away from the impulsive surface. Smooth-front regularizations of both profiles reproduce, at the calculated orders and away from the characteristic zero mode, the singular structure of the matched impulsive propagators without generating inverse transverse-momentum poles.

papers.title_en: First Light with the Dark100 Array of PANOSETI Telescopes at Palomar Observatory
papers.abstract_en: Dark100 is the first phase of an extensive array of Panoramic SETI (PANOSETI) telescopes at Palomar Observatory, California. PANOSETI telescopes are small, 0.5-m Fresnel lens telescopes instrumented with 1024-pixel silicon photomultiplier (SiPM) cameras. The telescopes were originally designed to search for ultra-fast optical transients, but they also function as cost-effective imaging atmospheric Cherenkov telescopes (IACTs). Dark100 will use seven of these widely separated IACTs to map the ultra-high-energy (UHE) gamma-ray sources on the Galactic Plane at high resolution. Dark100 will also leverage the IACT technique to search for evidence of ultra-heavy dark matter in a mass range that extends beyond 100 TeV. Deployment of the first four telescopes and enclosures was completed in December 2025, and commissioning of the next three is scheduled to finish by the end of 2026. The array has so far collected more than 100 hours of 3-telescope data on sources including the Crab Nebula and Markarian 421. Here we present the current status of Dark100.

papers.title_en: Pair-Condensation Peak in Radio-Frequency Dimer-Projection Spectroscopy of a Unitary Fermi Gas
papers.abstract_en: Radio-frequency dimer-projection spectroscopy has recently emerged as a powerful probe of strongly interacting Fermi gases, yet its frequency-resolved spectrum remains largely unexplored. Here we show that the spectrum exhibits two qualitatively distinct features: a broad quasiparticle continuum governed by fermionic pairing and a sharp pair-condensation peak arising from the coherent projection of condensed Cooper pairs onto the final-state dimer. To reveal this physics, we develop a point-dimer approximation that exploits the separation between the molecular and many-body length scales and expresses the radio-frequency response directly in terms of pair correlations in the initial many-body state. Within the BCS mean-field theory, we derive the frequency-dependent spectrum, identify the microscopic transfer processes underlying its structure, and show that the continuum possesses a threshold determined by the superfluid gap. Our theory establishes radio-frequency dimer-projection spectroscopy as a unified probe of short-range correlations, fermionic pairing, and long-range coherence in strongly interacting Fermi gases.

papers.title_en: Searching for gravitational wave echo with group equivariant neural posterior estimation
papers.abstract_en: Current methods for the gravitational-wave (GW) echo searches generally require substantial computational time and resources. Recent advances in group equivariant neural posterior estimation (GNPE) have demonstrated the potential to substantially accelerate posterior inference. In this work, we adopt this framework and train a GNPE model to perform echo searches, significantly improving computational efficiency while maintaining comparable inference accuracy. We apply it to the O4a events and find no significant evidence for the GW echo.

papers.title_en: The Geometric Crisis in Cygnus~X-3: Limitations of Wind-Fed Accretion and the Case for Roche-Lobe Overflow
papers.abstract_en: Cygnus~X-3 is a Galactic X-ray binary with a 4.8-hr orbital period operating in the ultraluminous regime. Although the system is viewed at relatively low inclination ($i\approx28^\circ$), it exhibits a deep orbital modulation. Recent IXPE observations show strong linear polarization orthogonal to the radio jet, indicating that the X-ray emission is dominated by reflection from the inner walls of a supercritical outflow funnel. We propose a Hybrid Roche-lobe overflow (RLOF) scenario in which a massive Wolf-Rayet donor effectively fills its Roche lobe with a focused wind driving a super-Eddington accretion stream. Using a numerical synthesis of the folded light curve, we show that the modulation is reproduced when the central funnel is periodically occulted by a vertically extended, shock-heated Turbulent Wall formed by stream impact on the outer disk rim. This produces a phase lag ($Δφ\approx0.11$) between X-ray minimum and binary conjunction, with extended attenuation by the WR wind defining a broader Suppression Region. This geometry explains the enhanced iron-line equivalent width during X-ray minimum via a coronagraphic effect. The large radial-velocity amplitude of FeXXVI measured by XRISM ($K_{\rm obs}\approx430$ km s$^{-1}$) and its zero-crossing at $φ_X=0.0$ arise naturally in the stream-impact region rather than from orbital motion of the compact object. Finally, we show that the observed secular orbital expansion ($\dot P>0$) follows directly from highly non-conservative mass transfer with inner-disk mass loss, indicating that Cygnus~X-3 is a stable, long-lived system in a supercritical accretion regime.

papers.title_en: Gamma-Ray Emission from LS 5039: A 30-500 GeV Excess and Phase-Resolved Broadband Spectral Modeling
papers.abstract_en: LS~5039 is a well-studied $γ$-ray binary exhibiting strong orbital modulation from GeV to TeV energies. We present a phase-resolved analysis of 17.3~yr of \textit{Fermi}-LAT observations and identify an additional $γ$-ray excess in the $\sim30$--$500$~GeV at a significance of $\sim7.9σ$. The phase-resolved spectra show pronounced orbital dependence above $\sim10$~GeV, with the inferior-conjunction more complex than the superior-conjunction. To investigate the broadband spectral energy distribution, we combine the \textit{Fermi}-LAT spectra with published H.E.S.S.\ and HAWC measurements and compare purely leptonic and lepto-hadronic models using the Bayesian information criterion. In both intervals, relativistic-Maxwellian and magnetospheric components dominate below $\sim10$~GeV, while shock-accelerated electrons account for much of the GeV--TeV continuum. The purely leptonic fits leave residuals at $30$--$500$~GeV and underpredict the HAWC measurements above $\sim100$~TeV. In the local one-zone intrabinary shock apex model, synchrotron cooling and Klein-Nishina suppression make the ultra-high-energy emission difficult to reproduce, although more complex leptonic scenarios remain possible. Adding a phenomenological proton component improves the broadband description, with stronger relative support during superior-conjunction than inferior-conjunction. However, the proton parameters remain weakly constrained and the fast-escape hadronic interpretation is energetically challenging, so a hadronic origin is not uniquely established. Future high-sensitivity, phase-resolved observations at multi-TeV and ultra-high energies will be required to test this interpretation.

papers.title_en: Long-term variability of the 35-day cycle in Her X-1
papers.abstract_en: Her X-1 is an eclipsing X-ray binary system consisting of an accreting neutron star and an optical component HZ Her. In addition to the 1.24-s X-ray pulsations and the 1.7-d orbital period, the system also shows a 35-day X-ray variability related to the precessional motion of a tilted and twisted accretion disk around the neutron star. The long-term persistence of the 35-day X-ray variability suggests the presence of a stable clock mechanism, most likely free precession of the magnetized neutron star. We have studied the long-term behavior of the 35-day cycle of Her X-1 using all available CGRO/BATSE, RXTE/ASM, Swift/BAT, Fermi/GBM, MAXI data and archival turn-on moments of the 35-day cycle spanning more than 50 years. We have used a sliding-window averaged X-ray phase light curve and the classical O-C (observed minus calculated) diagram for individual 35-day turn-ons to inspect the long-term trends of the O-C diagram. The O-C diagram demonstrates two similar parabolic trends separated by an anomalous low state (ALS) of the source suggesting a secular decrease in the 35-d precession period with $\dot P_\text{35} =(-1.3\pm0.2)\times10^{-5} \,\mathrm{~s\,s}^{-1}$ and $\dot P_\text{35} =(-4.7\pm0.1)\times10^{-5} \,\mathrm{~s\,s}^{-1}$ before and after the ALS, respectively. We conclude that the decay of the 35-day period as inferred from the O-C analysis can be interpreted in terms of the direct relationship between the change of the precessional period of the accretion disk to the long-term decrease of the period of the free precessional neutron star - due to continued accumulation of accreted matter.

papers.title_en: Vector modes in Type 3 New GR
papers.abstract_en: Some time ago, we published the full count of degrees of freedom in the linearised weak gravity limit of arbitrary New GR models. We did it by considering the linear weak gravity equations and presented a thorough analysis with no ambiguity left. A bit later, we generalised it to linear cosmological perturbations and discussed the strong coupling issues that appear already at this level. Recently, there were claims that some dynamical modes had been missed in our work. However, the authors of the new claims did not look at the equations of motion and analysed the quadratic Lagrangian densities instead. In this paper, I take one of the most elementary cases, namely the vector modes in New GR of Type 3, and show what was their mistake that had led them to claiming that those were dynamical. The main message: Do not substitute constraint equations into a Lagrangian.

papers.title_en: SN 2025dys: A luminous supernova explosion from a partially stripped helium star
papers.abstract_en: We present well-sampled multi-band imaging and low- to medium-resolution spectroscopic observations of the early-discovered Type~II supernova (SN)~2025dys. The photometric evolution exhibits a rise time of $\sim$\,18 days ($r$ band) and a rapid decline transitioning to the radioactive decay tail at $\sim$\,70 days. SN~2025dys is among the high-luminosity events with a peak pseudo-bolometric luminosity of $L_{\rm opt}=8.57\times10^{42}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$. Early X-ray emission was identified, displaying a luminosity of $7.55\times10^{40}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$. The observational investigation points to a dense, hydrogen-rich circumstellar medium with a mass of $M_{\rm CSM}\approx0.5$--$0.7\,\mathrm{M_\odot}$, suggesting a partially stripped, hydrogen-poor inner ejecta with a relatively low mass of $M_{\rm ej}\approx2.5\,\mathrm{M_\odot}$. The explosion possessed a kinetic energy of $E_{\rm k}\approx0.3\text{--}0.5$~foe and yielded a synthesized nickel mass of $M_{\rm Ni}\approx0.042_{-0.011}^{+0.012}\,\mathrm{M_\odot}$. These physical parameters indicate an extreme mass-loss episode before the explosion, characterized by a high mass-loss rate of $\dot{M} \gtrsim 0.01\,\mathrm{M_\odot\,yr^{-1}}$. SN~2025dys represents a stripped progenitor, intrinsically resembling a Type~IIb or even a Type~Ib SN, that exploded within a dense, hydrogen-rich circumstellar environment.

papers.title_en: The Phenomenology of the Dark Dimension and Non-Supersymmetric Strings
papers.abstract_en: Swampland principles, combined with the smallness of dark energy $Λ$, lead to the dark dimension scenario, with one extra dimension of micron size. We review this scenario and its predictions: KK graviton dark matter (or the KK tower of the quintessence field into which the gravitons convert), neutrino masses tied to $Λ^{1/4}$ via a bulk $B-L$ gauge symmetry, QCD axion decay constant $f_a\sim Λ^{1/12}\sim 10^9-10^{10}$ GeV at the 5d Planck scale $M_5$, connecting electroweak hierarchy to $Λ^{1/6}$, and a relation between the GUT and weak scales with $M_5$ as the geometric mean. The dark dimension also provides a concrete realization of an evolving dark sector: the evolution of its diameter correlates the variation of dark energy with that of the dark matter mass, fitting the recent DESI DR2 (+CMB+supernovae) data while avoiding the phantom crossing that the $w_0w_a$CDM parametrization would suggest---the apparent phantom behavior instead arises from the evolving dark matter mass. The fits suggest that the dark energy field sits in the interior of moduli space, near an unstable critical point. Motivated by this, we review recent progress on non-supersymmetric string vacua: isolated critical points protected by duality symmetries, in non-geometric flux compactifications and in Scherk--Schwarz compactifications of M-theory, and an emerging duality web for non-supersymmetric strings. This note is based on two talks given by the author at String Phenomenology 2026 (Paris) and Strings 2026 (Shanghai).

papers.title_en: Lattice Realizations of Flat Gauging and T-duality Defects at Any Radius
papers.abstract_en: We analyze non-invertible topological interfaces and defects in the two-dimensional compact boson, focusing on the more exotic ones obtained by gauging continuous symmetries with flat connections on a half-space. These include interfaces between mutually irrational radii and T-duality symmetries at arbitrary boson radius. Using the modified Villain discretization on both a Euclidean two-dimensional square lattice and a quantum one-dimensional chain, we show that all these topological interfaces survive discretization and give rise to non-compact edge modes localized at the defect sites. Such non-compact edge modes imply a continuous defect spectrum and an infinite quantum dimension. In the special case of rational radii, we show how the defect action or Hamiltonian can be modified in order to compactify the edge modes and produce more standard defects with finite quantum dimension.

papers.title_en: Graph-theory measures capture weak ergodicity breaking on large quantum systems
papers.abstract_en: We study the onset of weak ergodicity violations in closed quantum many-body systems and focus on cases in which they occur through a transition that is controlled by a model parameter, a scenario called a weak ergodicity-breaking transition. This situation is realized in the Rosenzweig-Porter model and the quantum sun model, which we investigate here. Our analysis is based on representing quantum systems in Fock space and examining the short-time dynamics of density autocorrelation functions. From these, we extract proxies for decay rates for each individual basis state. As a first main result, we show that the distribution of such decay rates captures known weak ergodicity-breaking transitions in both models. As a second main result, we establish a connection between the decay rates of density autocorrelations and graph-theoretical measures. Concretely, we demonstrate that moments of the distribution of the recently introduced graph-energy centrality also detect the weak ergodicity transitions, which is inherited from the behavior of the decay rates. While most numerical tools are limited to small system sizes, the quantities studied in our work can be calculated analytically for large systems of many hundreds of sites and in some cases, even in the thermodynamic limit.

papers.title_en: Interpretable Machine Learning for Building Analytic Quantum Circuits: the Case of Diagonal Operators
papers.abstract_en: Machine Learning has become a useful instrument across many fields, but the opacity of typical ``black-box'' models limits their value for scientific discovery. In this paper we present a methodology that uses \emph{interpretable} Machine Learning to generate analytic mathematical hypotheses about a physical system, which can then be confirmed by a formal derivation. We demonstrate the methodology on the problem of decomposing unitary operators into elementary quantum gates. By training an interpretable model on circuits obtained numerically and analyzing its weights, we are led to a hypothesis for the analytic structure of the decomposition. Applied to the family of diagonal operators, this hypothesis yields a universal, analytic quantum circuit valid for an arbitrary number of qubits, whose $CNOT$ count scales as $\mathcal{O}(2^n)$, improving on the $\mathcal{O}(2.5^n)$ of standard numerical methods. The resulting decomposition is proved rigorously in a companion paper.

papers.title_en: Pair density waves via interband pairing --- a perspective from superfluid weight
papers.abstract_en: Pair density waves (PDW) are superconducting states that exhibit a spatially modulated pairing order parameter, corresponding to Cooper pairs carrying finite center-of-mass momentum. While some recent studies have emphasized the role of quantum geometry in stabilizing PDW order in certain multiband systems, we here present a systematic investigation of an alternative, geometry-independent mechanism: PDW order driven purely by interband Cooper pairing. Using the superfluid weight (SW) as a diagnostic, we study two canonical models. The first is the classic Fulde-Ferrell model of an $s$-wave superconductor subject to a Zeeman splitting field, which realizes pure interband pairing between two rigidly shifted bands; the second is a spinless honeycomb-lattice model with nearest-neighbor $f$-wave pairing, a modified version of which was recently found to exhibit PDW instability in density-matrix renormalization-group simulations. In both models the SW receives no quantum geometric contribution at the mean-field level, yet it can be greatly suppressed or even turn negative, signaling a tendency toward pairing with spatial phase modulations. For the first model, we establish that the SW is increasingly suppressed as the Zeeman field grows, drastically turning negative upon the emergence of extensive gapless excitations, i.e., the Bogoliubov Fermi surfaces. For the honeycomb $f$-wave model, we demonstrate, both analytically and numerically, vanishing quantum-geometric SW and an invariably negative total SW. Our results thus establish the SW as a qualitative indicator of the tendency toward PDW order, and provide a microscopic rationale for the interband-pairing-driven PDW instability.

papers.title_en: Monodromy defects in ABJM theory and integrability
papers.abstract_en: We establish that supersymmetric monodromy defects in ABJM theory, also known as vortex loops, define integrable boundary states of the underlying alternating SU(4) spin chain. Exploiting the KT relation within the framework of the algebraic Bethe ansatz, we derive a closed-form expression for the leading-order one-point functions of non- protected operators in the presence of these defects. As a special case, our result reproduces the spin-chain overlap governing the three-point functions of two maximal giant gravitons and a single tiny graviton. We furthermore investigate the quantization of the theory in the defect background and compute the first quantum correction to the one-point functions in the simplest setting. Finally, we discuss possible extensions of our overlap formula.

papers.title_en: Witnessing Short- and Long-Range Nonstabilizerness via the Information Lattice
papers.abstract_en: We study nonstabilizerness on the information lattice and demonstrate that noninteger local information directly indicates nonstabilizerness. For states with a clear separation of short- and large-scale information, a noninteger total information at large scales $Γ$ serves as a witness of long-range nonstabilizerness. We propose a folding procedure to separate the global and edge-to-edge contributions to $Γ$. As an example we show that the ferromagnetic ground state of the spin-1/2 three-state Potts model has long-range nonstabilizerness originating from global correlations, while the paramagnetic ground state has at most short-range nonstabilizerness.

papers.title_en: Robustness of Starobinsky inflation in a minimal two-field scalar-tensor completion
papers.abstract_en: We investigate whether the Starobinsky inflation remains robust after including a minimal scalar extension motivated by the one-loop effective action of scalar-tensor gravity. We numerically solve the four-dimensional background system derived from the reduced slow-roll action and discover that the exact Starobinsky branch is a finite-time attractor in the sampled slow-roll domain when the additional scalar is at least as heavy as the scalaron. We derive quadratic actions for tensor and scalar modes and find a healthy kinetic sector with no scalar or tensor gradient instabilities. The propagation speeds are indistinguishable from the speed of light over the tested range of the derivative-coupling coefficient. These stability tests use the complete constraint-reduced quadratic operator over $|β|\leq1$, whereas the quoted production curvature spectra are obtained from the reduced scalar evolution. A direct complete-spectrum comparison in $β$, a separate complete--reduced regression at $β=0$, and independent bounds on the canonically normalised coefficient differences constrain the omitted derivative-coupling correction, including the numerical and CPU--GPU allowances, to at most $3.89488834\times10^{-7}$, below the $10^{-3}$ accuracy relevant to the physical conclusion. The curvature spectra remain extraordinarily close to the Starobinsky model across the entire parameter scan. Although the entropy-seeded mode can provide approximately one quarter of the final curvature power, removing the adiabatic--entropy mixing changes the total spectrum by only a few parts in a million, revealing nontrivial multifield dynamics behind an exceptionally robust observable prediction.

papers.title_en: New Effects in Multifield Cosmology Coupled to the Gauss-Bonnet Term
papers.abstract_en: We study the rapid-turn regime of multifield cosmology coupled to the Gauss-Bonnet term. We derive the corresponding modified relations between the inflationary Hubble and potential slow-roll parameters, in the two-field case. These relations show that including the Gauss-Bonnet coupling broadens the possibilities for realizing rapid turn inflation and for satisfying the swampland conjectures. We also derive a consistency condition relating the scalar field-space metric to the scalar potential and the Gauss-Bonnet coupling, which two-field slow-roll and rapid-turn inflationary solutions have to satisfy. Finally, we find general conditions under which phantom-like behavior is possible in multifield dark energy models coupled to the Gauss-Bonnet term. Notably, although we do not consider a direct interaction between dark matter and dark energy, dark matter is crucial for the occurrence of a phantom regime.

papers.title_en: New topological phase transitions in $κ$-deformed $φ^4$ lattice models
papers.abstract_en: This paper explores topological phase transitions in the momentum space of the $κ$-deformed $φ^4$ lattice model within the mean-field approximation. We show that the double-well structure of the momentum space gives rise to degenerate momentum states at high energies and that this change is marked by a phase transition. We investigate this transition using both numerical and analytical methods, with the analytical approach based primarily on singularity theory. Our numerical analysis shows that the energy at which the topological phase transition occurs is related to the noncommutative parameter by the simple power law $E \sim 1/α^{4}$. By mapping the constant-energy-level surface to the $A_{3}$ singularity, we obtain the same result analytically. We also present results unique to noncommutative systems, showing that the fraction of particles in degenerate momentum states has a nonzero commutative limit. As a nonperturbative effect, this result provides a testable prediction for the existence of noncommutative spacetime.

papers.title_en: Counting kinks and magnons with the lattice: magnetoelastic effects in Cs$_2$CoBr$_4$
papers.abstract_en: We report low-temperature dilatometry and ultrasound measurements on the frustrated quasi-one-dimensional antiferromagnet Cs$_2$CoBr$_4$ across the entire cascade of field-induced magnetic phase transitions. The whole phase diagram can be recovered from these lattice probes, with distinct anomalies observed at each phase boundary. Elongation along the principal chain axis is found to closely track magnetization throughout the phase diagram. This behavior is interpreted in terms of kinks in the Néel structure and magnons in the transverse-ordered magnetic-BEC phases, each carrying a fixed lattice distortion. A simultaneous analysis of ultrasound and striction data allows us to quantify the strength of magnetoelastic coupling.

papers.title_en: Lambda as a Probe of Lensing Consistency
papers.abstract_en: We introduce a framework to identify the radial transition in mass reconstruction reliability between strong and weak gravitational lensing in galaxy clusters. In weak lensing reconstruction, the convergence recovered from the reduced shear is subject to the mass-sheet degeneracy. We demonstrate that the degeneracy itself can serve as an indicator of the reconstruction reliability, and introduce a spatially resolved parameter $λ(r)$ to characterize this as a function of radius. We validate this approach on simulated clusters with realistic observational noise, and show that the radial behavior of $λ(r)$ captures the relative reliability of the two probes. Furthermore, when the global mass-sheet parameter $λ$ is constrained directly using strong lensing information, the tightest constraints arise where the two probes achieve comparable precision. This provides a quantitative basis for joint strong and weak lensing mass reconstruction.

papers.title_en: VINTERGATAN-GM: long-lived satellite planes induced by a massive GSE-like merger
papers.abstract_en: Satellite galaxies in the Local Group tend to be distributed in thin, planar configurations, with many sharing coherent orbital motion. Galaxy formation simulations in $Λ$CDM have historically struggled to produce similar structures, leading to the so-called "planes of satellites problem". In this work, we investigate whether the emergence of such structures is connected to the mass of a major merger at $z\sim2$, analogous to the Gaia-Sausage-Enceladus (GSE) event in the Milky Way. We use the VINTERGATAN-GM suite of high-resolution zoom-in simulations, comprising five realizations of the same Milky Way-mass halo generated through targeted genetic modifications of a GSE progenitor. The GSE-like merger mass ratio is systematically varied from 1:10 to 1:2.1, while keeping the final dynamical mass and large-scale environment fixed. We find a clear and consistent trend: more massive GSE-like mergers lead to satellite populations that are both more planar and more kinematically coherent. In particular, simulations with merger mass ratios larger than 1:6 develop Kinematic Persistent Planes (KPPs), in which at least 40% of satellites co-orbit around a common axis over extended periods, comparable to those observed in the Milky Way. These structures arise when sufficiently massive mergers, accreted along the direction of maximum compression of the Lagrangian volume, produce flattened host halos with anisotropic velocity dispersions aligned with the merger direction. The merger aligns the host halo's minor axis with the direction of flattening of the surrounding cosmic web, and planes of satellites then emerge through two complementary processes: (i) satellites preferentially infall along the host's equatorial plane, and (ii) anisotropic dynamical friction in the non-spherical halo gradually reshapes their orbits toward this plane, generating coherent and long-lived planar configurations.

papers.title_en: Bayesian inference of the dense matter equation of state built upon extended Skyrme interactions: A generalization
papers.abstract_en: The nonrelativistic theory of nuclear matter (NM) based on Brussels-Skyrme interactions is employed to develop models for dense and neutron-rich matter within a Bayesian framework. We employ the following set of constraints: the four best-known nuclear empirical parameters, the density dependence of the energy per particle in pure neutron matter (PNM), the density dependence of the Landau effective mass ($m_\mathrm{eff}$) of neutrons in PNM and symmetric NM, and a lower limit on the maximum gravitational mass that neutron stars (NSs) can support. In addition, a number of ``sanity checks'' are added: the values of the speed of sound, neutron and proton Landau effective masses, and Fermi velocities are constrained up to the central density of the most massive NS configuration and for isospin asymmetries $δ=(n_n-n_p)/(n_n+n_p)$ ranging from 0 to 1. Our ensemble of models \emph{fully} explores the capacity of nonrelativistic Brussels-Skyrme effective interactions to describe NM at densities exceeding several times the nuclear saturation density. This is a necessary step toward a better understanding of the properties of dense matter and possible correlations between the parameters of NSs and the parameters of NM. Due to the pronounced U-shaped density dependencies of $m_\mathrm{eff}$, which qualitatively agree with the predictions of ab initio calculations featuring three-body forces, all our models exhibit a non-monotonic ``rise-and-fall'' behavior of the thermal pressure ($p_\mathrm{th}$) as a function of density, which in extreme cases leads to $p_\mathrm{th} < 0$. This work is a generalization of [Beznogov and Raduta, Phys. Rev. C 110, 035805 (2024)].

papers.title_en: Quasinormal modes of thick branes in $f(R)$ gravity
papers.abstract_en: We systematically investigate the quasinormal modes of thick branes in $f(R)$ gravity by numerically solving the Schrödinger-like perturbation equation of gravitational perturbations. To ensure the reliability of the results, we employ three complementary methods: the asymptotic iteration method, the direct integration of the wave equation, and the time-domain numerical evolution. We analyze how the model parameters influence the shape of the effective potential of gravitational perturbations and find that the structure of the potential barrier plays a significant role in shaping the quasinormal frequency spectrum. The results obtained from the three methods exhibit strong consistency, thereby ensuring the reliability of the calculations. In particular, the real parts of the quasinormal frequencies exhibit an approximately arithmetic progression, suggesting that the quasi-localized states can be understood as resonances between the barriers.

papers.title_en: Novel thermodynamic topological subclass from inverse-temperature asymptotics
papers.abstract_en: We investigate the thermodynamic topology of the charged McGuigan--Nappi--Yost black hole in the canonical ensemble at fixed electric charge, identifying equilibrium black hole solutions as zeros of the thermodynamic vector field constructed from the generalized off-shell free energy. The inverse Hawking temperature diverges as the extremal limit is approached and approaches a finite positive value in the large-horizon limit. The zero points of the thermodynamic vector field reveal a thermodynamic phase structure consisting solely of a locally stable branch with positive winding number ($w=+1$). The innermost small black hole state is locally stable in the low-temperature limit. As the temperature increases, the stable branch extends toward the outermost large black hole regime, while no black hole states exist in the high-temperature regime beyond the finite upper Hawking temperature. This distinct asymptotic behavior of the inverse temperature places the thermodynamic defect structure outside the established topological (sub)classes, although its topological number agrees with that of the standard $W^{1+}$ class. We therefore identify this defect structure as a new thermodynamic topological subclass, $\breve W^{1+}$. This finding extends the existing classification to include a finite, nonzero large-horizon limit of the inverse Hawking temperature and suggests that distinct asymptotic behaviors in other black hole families may reveal further topological (sub)classes and thermodynamic phase structures.

papers.title_en: A Common Type II Origin of Galilean and Carroll Superstrings
papers.abstract_en: We show that the relativistic Type-II superalgebras, once the fundamental-string winding charge is retained alongside the momentum, admit a single non-Lorentzian contraction whose two translation ideals carry Galilean and magnetic-Carroll supersymmetry, respectively. The complementary vector charge required for this structure is thus intrinsic to string theory. The IIA realization is particle-like and the IIB realization string-like, a distinction fixed by chirality, and spacelike T-duality relates the two while preserving each non-Lorentzian structure. The same contraction is finite on the doubled Green--Schwarz action, including all fermion terms and local kappa symmetry, where the two supersymmetries appear as the two polarizations of a single worldsheet theory. These results unify two distinct non-Lorentzian corners of string theory within a common Type-II origin and open a route toward a broader web of non-Lorentzian dualities and possible holographic generalizations.

papers.title_en: Column-density estimation from the equivalent widths of absorption doublets
papers.abstract_en: Na I D absorption is widely used to estimate the dust extinction toward Galactic and extragalactic sources, but the inferred column densities are unreliable once the lines saturate. We present an analytical framework for estimating column densities from the equivalent widths ($EW$s) of absorption-line doublets. The method requires only that the two doublet members be measured separately -- the velocity structure need not be resolved -- so a resolving power $λ/Δλ\gtrsim10^{3}$ suffices for Na I D, two orders of magnitude below velocity-resolved methods. For the Gaussian curve of growth, the classical inversion reduces to a universal saturation correction depending only on the doublet ratio, $R=EW_2/EW_1$: at fixed $R$, the inferred column density is linear in the measured $EW$. The formulation yields the exact Gaussian inversion, $N_{\tildeκ}$, which provides the Doppler parameter; a closed-form second-order approximation; and a strict lower bound, $N_{\rm min}$, valid for an arbitrary velocity structure. We recommend reporting $N_{\rm min}$: an optimal, assumption-free lower bound, within a few per cent of $N_{\tildeκ}$ for $R\gtrsim1.4$ and at most a factor $3.5$ below it at $R=1.1$. The ratio $N_{\tildeκ}/N_{\rm 2nd}$ provides a per-object saturation diagnostic. We validate the framework against published profile-fitting Na I D column densities toward Type Ia supernovae, using only the integrated $EW$s. An explicit closed-form formula converts the two $EW$s into an extinction estimate through the observed $\log N(\mathrm{Na\,I})$--$A_V$ relation. A public implementation with full uncertainty propagation accompanies the paper.

papers.title_en: The pulsar population of Omega Centauri: New TRAPUM searches, timing, and cluster dynamics with MeerKAT and Parkes
papers.abstract_en: Millisecond pulsars (MSPs) are probes of globular clusters, tracing their stellar evolution, cluster dynamics, and gravitational potential. We searched for and timed MSPs in the Omega Centauri, then investigated their high-energy emission, the cluster potential, and MSP demographics. We performed Fourier-domain acceleration and jerk searches on MeerKAT observations, followed by pulsar timing using MeerKAT and Parkes Murriyang data spanning 2021-2025. We discovered the new isolated MSP PSR J1326-4728S (PSR S, Ps=4.538 ms and DM=96.24 pc/cm3. We updated the timing solutions for PSRs A-E, obtained the first timing solutions for G, H, and K, and updated the orbital parameters for I, L, N, and Q. The latter three, I, N, and Q, have significantly longer orbital periods (Pb=1-7 days) than previously reported. Pulsars B, G, H, K, and L are black widows (Pb=2-4 hours); I is a wide-orbit (Pb=3.50 days) MSP with a light ~0.05 Mo companion; N and Q have ~0.25 Mo companions; and N shows a significant orbital eccentricity (e=0.093). We folded Fermi-LAT and NICER photons to search for high-energy pulsations, but failed to detect them from individual MSPs. Significant spin period derivatives were measured for eight MSPs and interpreted as arising from the cluster gravitational potential. The inferred line-of-sight accelerations are consistent with a King-model gravitational potential, and allow us to set an upper central black hole mass limit of Mbh<8e4 Mo at 90% confidence. The high fraction of isolated MSPs (58%) and black widow systems (63% of binaries), and possibly the eccentricity of N, are difficult to reconcile with MSP population predictions based solely on encounter rates. Instead, these properties require alternative formation channels or reflect the complex evolutionary history of Omega Centauri, with part of its MSP population having formed in denser environments than those observed today.

papers.title_en: Reducing the cost of ancilla purification for Majorana quantum computation
papers.abstract_en: Braiding Majorana zero modes does not by itself provide a universal set of quantum gates. Additional operations can be supplied through ancillary states, whose preparation need not have the same protection as braiding. Here, we consider purification of the non-Gaussian ancilla used for an entangling gate in Bravyi's scheme. We keep his elementary braid-and-fusion comparison and change how its outputs are combined. An additional layer compares the product of the three stabilizer signs. The first accepted errors giving an incorrect output then require three faulty input blocks rather than two. As a result, the preparation error decreases cubically instead of quadratically, and the asymptotic raw-copy overhead is reduced. We also construct a preliminary sequence in which a processed block is paired with a fresh copy from the same noisy source. For independent inputs supported in the even-parity sector and ideal purification operations, this sequence establishes a sufficient distillability fidelity of 59.95 percent after free Gaussian twirling. At a common source fidelity, it reduces the expected cost of preparing an input for the recurrence by more than seven orders of magnitude relative to the balanced construction studied here. Finally, we examine imperfect purification operations in an effective syndrome-noise model. The additional layer leaves the leading operation-error coefficient unchanged, although a nonzero error floor remains.

papers.title_en: Prospects for Direct Detection of Ultralight Dark Matter candidates in deci-Hz Band with IndIGO-D
papers.abstract_en: We investigate the sensitivity of IndIGO-D, a proposed space-based decihertz gravitational-wave interferometer, to different classes of ultralight dark matter. IndIGO-D will probe the $\sim0.01$--$10~\mathrm{Hz}$ frequency band between those accessible to current ground- and future space-based gravitational-wave interferometers, providing access to ultralight dark-matter masses beyond the reach of existing instruments. We consider two complementary signatures: interferometric displacements induced by coherently oscillating scalar (dilaton), vector (dark-photon, $U(1)_B$ and $U(1)_{B-L}$ gauge groups), and tensor fields with masses $m_{\rm DM}\sim10^{-17}$--$10^{-14}~\mathrm{eV}$; and changes in laser polarization induced by pseudoscalar axion dark matter at higher masses, around $m_a\sim10^{-12}~\mathrm{eV}$. For the dilatons, dark photons and tensors, we compute the expected sensitivities using two pipelines -- cross-correlation and BSD excess-power -- assuming L-shaped and triangular interferometer layouts and three representative noise power spectral densities (S1, S2, S3), each for two years of continuous observation. We find that the projected sensitivities agree to within a factor of order unity across the search pipelines and interferometer geometries. In particular, we show that IndIGO-D could open previously unconstrained coupling parameter space for vector and tensor dark matter across $m_{\rm DM}\sim10^{-16}$--$10^{-14}~\mathrm{eV}$, bridging the sensitivity of space- and ground-based experiments. For axion dark matter, we demonstrate that a complementary detection for laser light polarization shifts, limited primarily by photon shot noise, could probe the axion-photon coupling $g_{aγ}$ at masses around $m_a\sim10^{-12}~\mathrm{eV}$ at a level potentially better than that of other future experiments without degrading sensitivity to gravitational waves.

papers.title_en: Phase transition dynamics of Abelian-Higgs vortices in the oscillating axion background
papers.abstract_en: We investigate the effect of an oscillating axion background on thermally induced vortex-antivortex production in the Abelian-Higgs model. Through its coupling to the gauge field, the axion sources an electromagnetic response in the presence of vortex magnetic flux, modifying the dynamics of the vortices. We study this system using Langevin lattice simulations with dissipation and stochastic noise. It is shown that the phase transition dynamics of Abelian-Higgs vortices, namely the pair creation of vortex and antivortex under thermal fluctuations, can be significantly modified in the oscillating axion background. We find that the axion background shifts the rapid increase in the vortex density to lower temperature. In particular, this transition temperature becomes smaller as the oscillation frequency of the axion increases. The temperature dependence of the correlation length is also modified. These features provide a new experimental approach for the axion dark matter using superconducting devices.

papers.title_en: Gravitational-Wave Sky Mapping with Pulsar Timing Arrays: The Full Earth-Pulsar Response and Resolution Operational Regimes
papers.abstract_en: Pulsar timing arrays (PTAs) are usually analyzed in the Earth-term approximation, although the exact response of an Earth--pulsar baseline contains additional angular structure through the pulsar term. We develop a tensor-spherical-harmonic framework for PTA sky mapping of a deterministic, band-limited gravitational-wave strain field, retaining the full Earth--pulsar response. The single-baseline response is reduced to a compact analytical closed form involving two spherical Bessel functions. Its asymptotic analysis reveals four regimes: Earth-term dominance, transition, pulsar-term dominance, and an effective diffraction cutoff at $l_\mathrm{cut}\simeqωL$. This scale characterizes the intrinsic exponential suppression of an individual baseline, while the practical angular resolution of a PTA is primarily governed by the finite number, sky distribution and timing noise of the pulsars. Formulating PTA sky mapping as a linear inverse problem; we derive the associated Fisher information matrix and construct an singular-value-decomposition-based reconstruction framework that explicitly separates observable and poorly constrained sky modes. The analysis clarifies the relationship between intrinsic detector resolution and array-sampling limitations and provides a quantitative assessment of the circumstances under which coherent pulsar-term information becomes relevant for full-sky reconstruction. Idealized scaling arguments suggest that exploiting the transition/pulsar-term-dominated regime in global sky mapping imposes a severe $\sim l^4$ penalty on the array size required to maintain uniform reconstruction fidelity at high multipoles. The formalism extends naturally to anisotropic stochastic backgrounds and provides a unified framework for deterministic field reconstruction and angular-power anisotropy inference.

papers.title_en: Suzuki-Trotter Decompositions and other Methods for Quantum Time Evolution
papers.abstract_en: (Suzuki-)Trotter decompositions, splitting methods, (Lie) product formulae... The most common numerical methods for the time evolution of quantum systems come with many names. And they are used practically everywhere with applications ranging from the solution of classical equations of motion and various Monte Carlo simulations to the real and imaginary time evolution on classical as well as quantum computers. Here we review the state of the art of said methods, focussing especially on the progress made over the last few years. We highlight recently discovered efficient time evolution algorithms and explain how best to use them in practice. A central part of this work is the estimation of error bounds that has improved greatly within the past decade. The relevance of time evolution methods for quantum computing is discussed with a focus on noisy hardware. Finally, a comprehensive overview of generalisations, related methods and alternatives to Trotterization is provided. This includes time-dependent Hamiltonian dynamics, processed methods, multi-product formulae, symplectic integrators, TDVP for tensor networks, quantum signal processing, Crouch-Grossman methods and more. The overall perspective in this work is that of a theoretical physicist. All mathematical proofs as well as some technical details are omitted for easier readability. Instead, this review serves as a hands-on guide and, of course, as a starting point for references that provide further details.

papers.title_en: Toward Quantum Utility in Correlated Topological Matter: Variational Preparation of Fractional Quantum Hall Manifolds
papers.abstract_en: We investigate the use of variational quantum algorithms to prepare and characterize fractional quantum Hall states on near-term quantum processors. Focusing on the $ν=1/3$ Laughlin phase described by the $V_1$ Haldane pseudopotential, we formulate the lowest-Landau-level problem in second quantization, and implement particle-number-preserving variational circuits combined with the variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) and variational quantum deflation (VQD). We benchmark the approach in two complementary geometries: Haldane sphere and torus shape. On the Haldane sphere, the target state is a unique zero-energy Laughlin ground state, providing a controlled test of the variational workflow and of excited-state reconstruction. On the torus, the problem retains the genuinely two-dimensional periodic character of the quantum Hall liquid and exhibits the threefold topological ground-state degeneracy expected for the $ν=1/3$ fractional filling factor. This feature makes the torus a more demanding benchmark than the quasi-one-dimensional cylinder or thin-torus limits commonly exploited in state-preparation quantum protocols. We benchmark the hardware-optimized variational states against exact diagonalization using energy estimates, error-mitigated observables, and subspace-containment diagnostics. Our results show that hybrid quantum algorithms can approximately reconstruct the low-energy structure of small fractional quantum Hall systems, including the topological ground-state manifold on the torus. Beyond serving as a benchmark for quantum hardware, this geometry-resolved approach provides a route toward quantum simulations of fractional Chern insulators and strongly correlated topological phases in realistic two-dimensional materials.

papers.title_en: The hadronic-vacuum-polarization contribution to the muon anomalous magnetic moment in isospin-symmetric lattice QCD with twisted-mass fermions
papers.abstract_en: We present a lattice-QCD calculation of the leading-order hadronic-vacuum-polarization (HVP) contribution to the anomalous magnetic moment of the muon in isospin-symmetric QCD. We employ the gauge configurations generated by the Extended Twisted Mass Collaboration (ETMC) with $N_f = 2 + 1 + 1$ flavors of Wilson-clover twisted-mass quarks at four lattice spacings and at values of the quark-mass parameters matching the definition of isospin-symmetric QCD given in the FLAG review 2024 and in the 2025 edition of the Muon $g-2$ Theory Initiative White Paper (WP25). After retuning the simulation parameters to precisely match these two definitions of isospin-symmetric QCD, and after carrying out an extrapolation to the continuum limit based on the data at lattice spacings $a \simeq 0.049, 0.057, 0.068$ and $0.079$~fm, and spatial lattice sizes up to $L \simeq 7.7$~fm, we obtain $a_μ^{\rm HVP, FLAG}(\rm{iso}) = (720.0 \pm 6.9) \times 10^{-10}$ and $a_μ^{\rm HVP, WP25}(\rm{iso}) = (714.8 \pm 7.4) \times 10^{-10}$. Our results, which have a relative uncertainty of about $1 \%$, agree well with the corresponding determinations by other lattice groups. After adding to our determination of $a_μ^{\rm HVP, WP25}(\rm{iso})$ the leading isospin-breaking corrections provided in the WP25, namely $a_μ^{\rm HVP, WP25}({\rm IB}) = 0.1(3.4)\times 10^{-10}$, we obtain for the full HVP the value $a_μ^{\rm HVP}= (714.9 \pm 8.1)\times 10^{-10}$. This result translates into a Standard Model prediction for the muon anomalous magnetic moment that is fully consistent with the latest result by the Fermilab Muon $g-2$ experiment and strengthens the tension between lattice QCD and data-driven (pre-CMD3) dispersive determinations.

papers.title_en: Complete characterization of internal-external entanglement trade-offs in two-mode Gaussian states
papers.abstract_en: We characterize the exact trade-off between internal and external entanglement in asymmetric two-mode Gaussian states at fixed local symplectic eigenvalues. Internal entanglement is quantified by the negativity $\mathcal{N}_{A:B}$ between the two modes, while external entanglement is quantified by the negativity $\mathcal{N}_{AB:CD}$ across a Gaussian purification. Numerical sampling suggests the boundary structure of the attainable region in the $(\mathcal{N}_{AB:CD},\mathcal{N}_{A:B})$ plane, which we then determine analytically. Parametrizing the global symplectic spectrum yields a closed admissible interval for the remaining spectral parameter at fixed $\mathcal{N}_{AB:CD}$. We prove constructively that every point in this interval corresponds to a physical covariance matrix, implying that all intermediate values of $\mathcal{N}_{A:B}$ between the resulting sharp bounds are achievable. The upper bound is attained for opposite-sign correlations of equal magnitude, while the positive branch of the lower bound occurs when one global symplectic eigenvalue equals unity. We also identify two external-entanglement thresholds, derive a saturated monogamy-type inequality, and recover the symmetric-state limit. Because the external negativity depends only on the spectrum of the reduced two-mode state, the bounds hold for any purification, including non-Gaussian purifications.

papers.title_en: World-Line Actions in Weyl Geometry
papers.abstract_en: In this note we construct, from a gauge theory perspective, the world-line action for a particle moving on a time-like curve in Weyl geometry. The action we find is dimensionless, Weyl invariant, additive and, in general, non-local due to an open Wilson line which we have to add in order to account for a general Weyl field. In special cases, this Wilson line can be local, but the geometry becomes integrable. The action can not be used to measure the proper time as it is dimensionless and no mass parameter is allowed in the symmetric phase of the theory. We show that the usual conditions for defining proper time: affine parametrization, dimension of time and additivity supplemented by the requirement of Weyl invariance can not be fulfilled simultaneously and therefore no satisfactory notion of proper time exists in the symmetric phase. Under spontaneous symmetry breaking the particle acquires a mass, the action becomes Riemannian and the proper time can be again defined. We also construct a classically equivalent quadratic action by using an einbein on the world-line and show that the non-locality can be seen to arise from integrating out a constrained field.

papers.title_en: Reprocessing of X-rays emission in Ultra-Luminous X-ray sources
papers.abstract_en: Most of the Ultraluminous X-ray Sources (ULXs) harbor either a neutron star or a stellar-mass black hole as a compact object accreting at super-Eddington rates. In spite of having such a high accretion rate, the reprocessed emission in ULXs is quite meagre compared to that observed in Galactic X-ray binaries, except for some absorption lines in the winds. In this work, we use archival Chandra and \xmm\ observations to investigate the extent of reprocessed emission in ULXs through three diagnostics: (i) searches for Fe $\rm Kα$ lines in bright well-known ULXs and Ultraluminous X-ray Pulsars (ULXPs), (ii) evolution of hardness ratio around the eclipse transitions in the eclipsing ULXs, and (iii) the flux ratio between eclipse and out-of-eclipse (OOE) phases in eclipsing ULXs. We constrain the equivalent width (EW) of the Fe K$α$ line, with upper limits of $\sim$11-20 eV for a fixed line centroid (6.4 keV) and width (0.1 keV). Allowing the centroid and width to vary yields more conservative upper limits of up to $\sim$50 eV. Furthermore, we have not observed any significant changes in the hardness ratio in eclipsing ULXs during ingress or egress, whereas in Galactic eclipsing X-ray binaries the hardness ratio increases during the transitions. Finally, the reprocessing efficiency (eclipse-to-OOE flux ratio) is found to be larger in ULXs compared to Galactic eclipsing X-ray binaries. Based on these results, we discuss the possibility of a metal-poor or highly ionized environment surrounding the ULXs, which suppresses reprocessed emission features.

papers.title_en: eCAS: An Orbital Embedding Method for Quantum Computing
papers.abstract_en: Future fault-tolerant quantum computers will allow us to calculate electronic structures of atomistic systems. However, these systems will be intrinsically limited in size, requiring embedding theories for many systems because of the unfavorable scaling of the number of terms describing the electron-electron interaction in the second-quantized electronic Hamiltonian. Quantum embedding theories address this challenge by partitioning a quantum system into a region of interest, the impurity, and its (larger) complement, the environment. However, currently available quantum embedding methods place restrictive demands on near-future quantum computers, such as the need to measure reduced density matrices or the need for repeated evaluations. Here, we introduce the new orbital embedding method eCAS that steers clear of these pitfalls by constructing a multi-CAS problem, the active spaces of which are localized and can be solved independently of each other with any quantum algorithm. This also allows for the development of comparatively simple gradient expressions. eCAS leverages the Schmidt decomposition to construct initial impurity and bath orbitals and augments them with localized environment orbitals, based on a mutual correlation criterion. The mutual correlation criterion makes eCAS systematically improvable without the need for any iteratively determined quantities.

papers.title_en: Disk-Corona Energy Balance Evolves with Flux State in the Quasar PDS 456
papers.abstract_en: We investigate the long-term X-ray spectral evolution of the highly luminous, radio-quiet quasar PDS 456 using AstroSat observations obtained in 2019 and 2021 together with archival XMM-Newton, NuSTAR and Suzaku observations spanning 2001-2024. The AstroSat observations provide valuable coverage following the bright flaring state observed in 2018, revealing that the source underwent a relatively quiescent phase in 2019 before re-brightening in 2021. During the AstroSat epochs, PDS 456 exhibits a harder-when-brighter spectral trend, whereas the long-term XMM-Newton, NuSTAR, and Suzaku observations confirm the overall softer-when-fainter behavior. This behavior is consistent with the presence of a very cool corona (~15 keV), possibly driven by a strong incident photon field for upscattering, as suggested by a prominent big blue bump. Broadband spectral modeling of simultaneous XMM-Newton and NuSTAR observations, complemented by the 2021 AstroSat flaring epoch and interpreted within the self-consistent physical framework reXcor, indicates that the disk-corona energy balance evolves with flux. In low-flux states, the spectrum is reflection-dominated, implying efficient illumination of the inner accretion disk by a compact corona. In contrast, high-flux states show an enhanced contribution from the warm Comptonizing region at larger coronal heights. The Fe Kα emission line displays a positive correlation with the 2-10 keV continuum flux at low to intermediate flux levels, while deviations at the highest flux states suggest a reduced relative reflection contribution as the warm corona becomes energetically dominant.

papers.title_en: Resonant transmission of scalar waves through rotating traversable wormhole
papers.abstract_en: The viability of traversable wormholes as exotic compact objects relies on identifying signatures that distinguish them from black holes and other compact objects. In this work, we investigate the propagation of a massless scalar field in a rotating traversable wormhole described by Teo's class of solutions. We compute the greybody factor (transmissivity) and identify sharp Breit-Wigner-type resonances associated with scalar modes trapped in the potential well surrounding the throat. Rotation modifies these resonances through frame dragging, with counter rotating modes developing deeper trapping wells. We further investigate the stability of the long lived resonant modes through their quasinormal mode spectrum and find that corotating modes exhibit ergoregion instability. We therefore focus on the partial transmission cross section of the stable counter rotating modes, which characterizes the resonant transmission of incident scalar flux through the wormhole to the other asymptotic region. Our findings establish the role of rotation and mode stability in shaping the resonant transmission of scalar waves through traversable wormholes, providing a basis for future studies of analogous resonant phenomena in electromagnetic and gravitational waves, and their potential observational implications.

papers.title_en: Probing Realistic Neutron Star Equations of State via the Chameleon Mechanism
papers.abstract_en: We investigate the impact of the Chameleon mechanism on structural properties of neutron stars adopting realistic nucleonic equations of state. The scalar-matter coupling parameter $β$ controls the departure from the corresponding general-relativistic configurations, affecting both the maximum mass and the stellar radius. Our numerical results demonstrate that the chameleon mechanism can have a significant impact on the macroscopic properties of neutron stars, even when realistic equations of state are employed. Moreover, well established constraints on masses and radii of neutron stars put stringent limits on the allowed numerical values of the coupling.

papers.title_en: Quantum Popcorn: the shape of a phase transition bubble
papers.abstract_en: A quantum tunneling event in field theory is usually depicted as the materialization of a spherical bubble of true vacuum. The bubble appears at rest, and its profile is the time-symmetric slice of Coleman's bounce, the Euclidean solution that controls the decay rate. However, the bubble is spherical only in the leading semiclassical approximation: at the next order the configuration is a Gaussian ensemble of fluctuations around the bounce. We derive the wave functional of the field on the nucleation slice from the half-bounce path integral, and use it to compute the root-mean-square quadrupole moment of a bubble at nucleation. The relative deformation of the bubble wall radius $R$ is $δR/R\sim(\hbar/S_b)^{1/2}$, with $S_b$ the bounce action. Thus $δR/R\sim0.1$ for a typical cosmological phase transition with $S_b/\hbar\sim100$.

papers.title_en: As a matter of reconstruction -- varying the magnetic Prandtl number in implicit large eddy simulations
papers.abstract_en: The magnetic Prandtl number ($\mathrm{Pm}$), the ratio of viscosity to magnetic diffusivity, spans many orders of magnitude in astrophysical plasmas. It shapes how turbulence amplifies and structures magnetic fields. In direct numerical simulations (DNS) the viscosity and magnetic diffusivity can be controlled explicitly and independently, whereas in implicit large eddy simulations (ILES) they are set by the numerical scheme. We test whether, in a finite-volume code, $\mathrm{Pm}$ can be varied through the reconstruction scheme by applying different methods to the hydro and magnetic variables. As a proof of concept, we simulate driven, subsonic, homogeneous magnetohydrodynamic turbulence using five pairs of hydrodynamic and magnetic reconstruction schemes at varying resolutions. We measure the effective viscosity and resistivity from the energy transfer between scales. Reconstructing the magnetic field at higher order than the fluid raises the effective magnetic Prandtl number and vice versa. We demonstrate that a mix of second- and third-order reconstruction alone results in a $\gtrsim20\times$ change in $\mathrm{Pm}$. A comparison of DNS with matched explicit dissipation at these values agrees with the ILES. Mixed reconstruction thus offers a simple and efficient way to explore $\mathrm{Pm} \not\simeq 1$ in ILES without adding explicit dissipation.

papers.title_en: OASIS III: Bursty star formation drives observed galaxy sizes at $z\geq4$
papers.abstract_en: We employ JWST/NIRSpec MSA PRISM spectroscopy together with NIRCam imaging to investigate the impact of star-formation variability on galaxy sizes for a representative sample of 51 galaxies at $z\geq4$. The OASIS survey enables us to probe low-star-formation-rate (SFR) lulling and mini-quenched galaxies down to $\log_{10}(M_\star/M_\odot)=8.3$ and $\log_{10}(\mathrm{SFR}/M_\odot\,\mathrm{yr}^{-1})<-1.6$, i.e. more than one order of magnitude below the star-forming main sequence (MS). This enables us to probe objects that are often missed by shallower spectroscopic surveys, in addition to the MS and starburst systems, yielding an SFR- and mass-representative sample at high redshift. We derive galaxy half-light sizes using ForcePho, enabling us to resolve the highly compact nature of these sources, and we analyse their star-formation histories and interstellar medium (ISM) properties with the full-spectral-fitting code ppxf. We find a clear anti-correlation between burstiness, as traced by the ratio of the SFR from H$α$ compared to that from non-parametric spectral fitting averaged over 100 Myr, and galaxy UV/optical half-light radii as measured with ForcePho from a combination of well-sampled NIRCam photometry. Using partial correlation coefficients we show that the anti-correlation between burstiness (as traced by the SFR ratio) and size cannot simply be explained by secondary dependencies on stellar mass or redshift. We interpret this relation as the effect of central starbursts in SFR-rising (bursting) systems, where intense central star formation reduces measured galaxy half-light sizes. This burstiness then regulates galaxy sizes at high redshift. Should the same mechanism be present at $z>10$, this could explain the size bimodality seen in the UV luminous galaxies as simply stemming from a more fundamental relationship between burstiness and size.

papers.title_en: Wide-field search for submicrosecond optical and gamma transients as manifestation of primordial black holes evaporation with the TAIGA-HiSCORE Cherenkov array
papers.abstract_en: We demonstrated in our papers [Panov, 2021; Panov,2025), that the TAIGA-HiSCORE Cherenkov array physics, originally designed for research in cosmic rays and ultra-high-energy gamma-ray astronomy, can also be used for wide-field searches for very rare submicrosecond optical transients of astrophysical origin. The papers \cite{PANOV-2021,PANOV-2025} presented the results of the first four seasons of optical transient searches (2018--2022) and the resulting upper limits on the flux of corresponding events. The present paper presents data processing from two new seasons of optical transient searches (2022--2024). This paper further develops a method for searching for narrow spatiotemporal groups of ultra-high-energy gamma-rays (above 100\,TeV). Since the evaporation of relic black holes can be accompanied by both by the emission of a short light pulse and by a flash of ultra-high-energy gamma-rays, a multimessenger technique for searching for black hole evaporation was in fact implemented in this work, where two different methods are implemented within a single instrument. The search for narrow spatiotemporal groups of gamma-rays was carried out in time windows of 1000\,$μ$s, 100\,$μ$s, and 6\,$μ$s. Since narrow groups of gamma were not detected, the upper limit on their frequency were obtained as $10^{-3}\,\mathrm{ster}^{-1}\mathrm{h}^{-1}$. The upper limit on the number of submicrosecond optical transients have also been updated: $10^{-4}\mathrm{erg/s/cm}^2$ as $5\cdot10^{-4}\,\mathrm{ster}^{-1}\mathrm{h}^{-1}$.

papers.title_en: Enhanced Detectability of Very-High-Energy Gamma Rays from Off-Axis Short Gamma-Ray Bursts: Impacts of Structured Jets and External Inverse-Compton Scattering
papers.abstract_en: The binary neutron star merger GW170817 established a direct link between gravitational waves and short gamma-ray bursts (sGRBs), whose afterglows are commonly interpreted as nonthermal emission from structured relativistic jets viewed off-axis. Some sGRBs exhibit extended or plateau X-ray emission, suggesting prolonged central-engine activity. These X-ray photons can serve as seed photons for external inverse-Compton (EIC) scattering by relativistic electrons in the jet, producing very-high-energy (VHE) gamma rays. However, how the angular structure of the jet affects the detectability of EIC emission remains insufficiently explored. Here, we investigate EIC emission from off-axis structured jets and assess its detectability with the Cherenkov Telescope Array Observatory (CTAO). We find that EIC emission powered by extended and/or plateau X-rays produces detectable VHE signals from nearby sGRBs, particularly during the early afterglow, significantly outshining synchrotron self-Compton emission. In our adopted models, Gaussian and power-law jets produce brighter off-axis EIC emission than a top-hat jet, extending the viewing-angle range over which VHE emission may be detectable. These results demonstrate that early VHE observations with CTAO can probe both prolonged central-engine activity and the angular structure of relativistic jets in sGRBs.

papers.title_en: Early- and late-time constraints on Wald-Gauss-Bonnet topological dark energy and implications for the $H_0$ and $S_8$ tensions
papers.abstract_en: The persistent $H_0$ and $S_8$ tensions motivate the search for new dark-energy mechanisms capable of modifying the late-time expansion history while preserving the successful early-Universe predictions of $Λ$CDM scenario. Wald-Gauss-Bonnet (WGB) topological dark energy provides a physically motivated realization of this possibility, where the effective dark-energy sector emerges from cosmic horizon thermodynamics and the black-hole formation and merger history. We present the first early- and late-Universe analysis of WGB cosmology, implementing the model as an effective fluid in a modified \texttt{CLASS} solver and constraining it against CMB data from \textit{Planck}, ACT~DR6 and SPT-3G, DESI~DR2 BAO, and Pantheon+ supernovae. While late-time data alone are consistent with $Λ$CDM, the full dataset prefers a non-zero WGB contribution, $\Cn=0.387^{+0.118}_{-0.072}$, corresponding to a $>3σ$ phantom-like deviation and an improved fit ($Δχ^2=-10.3$). The preferred solution raises $H_0$ from $68.5$ to $69.8~\kmsmpc$, reducing the Hubble tension by $\sim1σ$, at the cost of a mild increase in $S_8$. The reconstructed cosmological observables show that WGB leaves the primary CMB almost unchanged while enhancing lensing and small-scale clustering, revealing a characteristic $H_0$-$S_8$ trade-off. WGB dark energy therefore emerges as a physically motivated and observationally viable late-time mechanism for partially alleviating the Hubble tension without introducing new early-Universe physics.

papers.title_en: Probing dark sector with decihertz gravitational wave observations of compact binary inspirals in IndIGO-D
papers.abstract_en: We investigate the potential of decihertz gravitational-wave (GW) observations of compact-binary inspirals to probe atomic dark matter (aDM) and its interactions through an ultralight massive dark photon. We consider a scenario in which neutron stars accumulate DM charged under a dark Abelian massive vector mediator, leading to an additional long-range Yukawa interaction between compact objects and associated dipolar radiation. In this framework, the GW waveform acquires characteristic corrections parameterized by the Yukawa coupling strength $α$, the dipole-radiation parameter $γ$, and a parameter related to the mediator mass $μ$. These corrections include a leading $-1$ post-Newtonian dipole contribution and finite-mediator-mass effects. We relate the aDM corrections to existing parameterized tests of general relativity and perform Bayesian parameter-estimation analyses for simulated binary neutron star (BNS) and neutron star-black hole (NSBH) systems incorporating the modified binary inspiral in a proposed space-based decihertz detector, named IndIGO-D. For a GW170817-like BNS with nonzero aDM couplings chosen near current observational bounds, we find that the dark-photon rest energy can be inferred with a $90\%$ credible uncertainty of $O(10^{-20})\,\mathrm{eV}$, conditional on a detectable dark-sector contribution. Analyses with weaker dark-sector interactions $(α\lesssim O(10^{-8}))$ show that the mediator mass remains unconstrained when both the Yukawa coupling and dipole-radiation contribution are negligible, but can be measured even for a negligible Yukawa coupling if the dipole-radiation contribution is sufficiently strong.
